source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public 9:1 = Isa 8:23; public 9:2–21 = Isa 9:1–20. All other labels match.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Preserve prophet, father, geography, four kings.
verses.before: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
verses.after: The vision Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

verses.rationale: Retain cosmic summons and parental accusation.
verses.before: Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for the LORD has spoken: I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.
verses.after: Hear, heavens! Listen, earth! The **LORD** has spoken: “I raised children and brought them up, but they rebelled against me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for the LORD has spoken: I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.

verses.rationale: Preserve two animals and knowing refrain.
verses.before: The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master's crib; but Israel does not know, my people do not consider.
verses.after: An ox knows its owner, a donkey its master’s feeding trough, but Israel does not know; my people do not understand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master's crib; but Israel does not know, my people do not consider.

verses.rationale: Retain family indictment and Holy One title.
verses.before: Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with iniquity, a seed of evil-doers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD. They have despised the Holy One of Israel. They are estranged and backward.
verses.after: Alas, sinful nation, people weighed down with guilt, offspring of evildoers, corrupt children! They have abandoned the **LORD**, scorned the Holy One of Israel, and turned their backs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with iniquity, a seed of evil-doers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken the LORD. They have despised the Holy One of Israel. They are estranged and backward.

verses.rationale: Keep bodily metaphor and questions.
verses.before: Why should you be beaten more, that you revolt more and more? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
verses.after: Why invite more blows? Why keep rebelling? The whole head is sick, the whole heart faint.
verses.tsw_comparator: Why should you be beaten more, that you revolt more and more? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.

verses.rationale: Retain untreated injuries and three negatives.
verses.before: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it: wounds, welts, and open sores. They have not been closed, neither bandaged, neither soothed with oil.
verses.after: From the sole of the foot to the head, no part is sound— wounds, bruises, raw sores, not cleaned, not bandaged, not soothed with oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it: wounds, welts, and open sores. They have not been closed, neither bandaged, neither soothed with oil.

verses.rationale: Keep devastation and witnessed consumption.
verses.before: Your country is desolate. Your cities are burned with fire. Strangers devour your land in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
verses.after: Your country is desolate; your cities have burned. Foreigners devour your land before your eyes; it is desolate, overthrown by strangers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your country is desolate. Your cities are burned with fire. Strangers devour your land in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.

verses.rationale: Preserve daughter personification and three similes.
verses.before: The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a besieged city.
verses.after: Daughter Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, a hut in a cucumber field, a city under siege.
verses.tsw_comparator: The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a besieged city.

verses.rationale: Retain remnant and named cities.
verses.before: Unless the LORD of Hosts had left to us a very small remnant, we would have been as Sodom; we would have been like Gomorrah.
verses.after: Had the **LORD** of hosts not left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, like Gomorrah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Unless the LORD of Hosts had left to us a very small remnant, we would have been as Sodom; we would have been like Gomorrah.

verses.rationale: Preserve accusatory renamed audience and instruction.
verses.before: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
verses.after: Hear the **LORD**’s word, rulers of Sodom! Listen to our God’s instruction, people of Gomorrah!
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

verses.rationale: Keep complete sacrificial animal list.
verses.before: "What are the multitude of your sacrifices to me?," says the LORD. "I have had enough of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed animals. I do not delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats.
verses.after: “What do I want with all your sacrifices?” says the **LORD**. “I have had enough burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed animals. I take no pleasure in the blood of bulls, lambs, or male goats.
verses.tsw_comparator: "What are the multitude of your sacrifices to me?," says the LORD. "I have had enough of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed animals. I do not delight in the blood of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats.

verses.rationale: Retain presence and trampling question.
verses.before: When you come to appear before me, who has required this at your hand, to trample my courts?
verses.after: When you come to appear before me, who asked you to trample my courts?
verses.tsw_comparator: When you come to appear before me, who has required this at your hand, to trample my courts?

verses.rationale: Preserve ritual terms and ethical conjunction.
verses.before: Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me; new moons, Sabbaths, and convocations: I cannot bear with evil assemblies.
verses.after: Bring no more empty offerings! Your incense disgusts me. New moons, Sabbaths, summoned assemblies— I cannot bear wrongdoing joined to solemn gatherings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me; new moons, Sabbaths, and convocations: I cannot bear with evil assemblies.

verses.rationale: Retain divine hatred and burden imagery.
verses.before: My soul hates your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They are a burden to me. I am weary of bearing them.
verses.after: I hate your new moons and appointed festivals. They have become a burden; I am tired of carrying them.
verses.tsw_comparator: My soul hates your New Moons and your appointed feasts. They are a burden to me. I am weary of bearing them.

verses.rationale: Keep prayer posture and bloody hands.
verses.before: When you spread forth your hands, I will hide my eyes from you. Yes, when you make many prayers, I will not hear. Your hands are full of blood.
verses.after: When you spread out your hands, I will hide my eyes from you. Even if you multiply prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are full of blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you spread forth your hands, I will hide my eyes from you. Yes, when you make many prayers, I will not hear. Your hands are full of blood.

verses.rationale: Retain bodily washing and ethical commands.
verses.before: Wash yourselves, make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil.
verses.after: Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean. Remove your evil deeds from my sight. Stop doing evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wash yourselves, make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes. Cease to do evil.

verses.rationale: Keep distinct legal actions and difficult oppression phrase.
verses.before: Learn to do good; seek justice, correct oppression; bring justice to the orphan, plead the widow’s cause.
verses.after: Learn to do good. Seek justice. Set oppression right. Defend the fatherless; plead the widow’s case.
verses.tsw_comparator: Learn to do good; seek justice, correct oppression; bring justice to the orphan, plead the widow’s cause.

verses.rationale: Preserve judicial invitation and two color contrasts.
verses.before: “Come now, and let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will become white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they will become like wool.
verses.after: “Come now, let us settle the matter,” says the **LORD**. “Though your sins are scarlet, they shall be white as snow; though red as crimson, they shall become like wool.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Come now, and let us reason together,” says the LORD. “Though your sins are like scarlet, they will become white as snow; though they are red like crimson, they will become like wool.

verses.rationale: Retain conditional willing obedience and eating.
verses.before: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the good of the land;
verses.after: If you are willing and listen, you will eat the land’s good produce.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you are willing and obedient, you will eat the good of the land;

verses.rationale: Keep eat/be-eaten wordplay and closing authority.
verses.before: but if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured with the sword; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken it."
verses.after: But if you refuse and rebel, the sword will eat you.” The mouth of the **LORD** has spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: but if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured with the sword; for the mouth of the LORD has spoken it."

verses.rationale: Retain sexual city metaphor and lodging contrast.
verses.before: How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice; righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers.
verses.after: How the faithful city has become a prostitute! Once she was full of justice; righteousness lodged in her— but now, murderers.
verses.tsw_comparator: How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice; righteousness lodged in her, but now murderers.

verses.rationale: Keep two adulterated substances.
verses.before: Your silver has become dross, your wine mixed with water.
verses.after: Your silver has become dross; your drink is diluted with water.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your silver has become dross, your wine mixed with water.

verses.rationale: Preserve systemic corruption and excluded litigants.
verses.before: Your princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves. Everyone loves bribes, and follows after rewards. They do not judge the orphan, neither does the cause of the widow come to them.
verses.after: Your rulers are rebels, partners of thieves. Every one loves a bribe and chases rewards. They do not defend the fatherless; the widow’s case never reaches them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves. Everyone loves bribes, and follows after rewards. They do not judge the orphan, neither does the cause of the widow come to them.

verses.rationale: Retain three divine titles and vengeance.
verses.before: So the Lord GOD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, says: "Ah, I will get relief from my adversaries, and avenge myself of my enemies;
verses.after: Therefore the Lord, the **LORD** of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: “Ah, I will find relief from my adversaries and take vengeance on my enemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel, says: "Ah, I will get relief from my adversaries, and avenge myself of my enemies;

verses.rationale: Keep purification as hostile hand and metallurgy.
verses.before: and I will turn my hand on you, thoroughly purge away your dross, and will take away all your tin.
verses.after: I will turn my hand against you, smelt away your dross as with lye, and remove all your alloy.
verses.tsw_comparator: and I will turn my hand on you, thoroughly purge away your dross, and will take away all your tin.

verses.rationale: Retain restored institutions and two names.
verses.before: I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you will be called 'The city of righteousness, a faithful town.'
verses.after: I will restore your judges as at first, your counselors as in the beginning. Afterward you will be called City of Righteousness, Faithful City.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. Afterward you will be called 'The city of righteousness, a faithful town.'

verses.rationale: Keep redemption and returning ambiguity noted.
verses.before: Zion will be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.
verses.after: Zion will be redeemed through justice, and those who return to her through righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: Zion will be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.

verses.rationale: Retain combined judgment and abandoning relation.
verses.before: But the destruction of transgressors and sinners will be together, and people who forsake the LORD will be consumed.
verses.after: But rebels and sinners will be shattered together; those who abandon the **LORD** will come to an end.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the destruction of transgressors and sinners will be together, and those who forsake the LORD will be consumed.

verses.rationale: Preserve third/second-person shift and cultic landscapes.
verses.before: For they will be ashamed of the oaks which you have desired, and you will be confounded for the gardens that you have chosen.
verses.after: They will be ashamed of the mighty trees you desired; you will blush for the gardens you chose.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they will be ashamed of the oaks which you have desired, and you will be confounded for the gardens that you have chosen.

verses.rationale: Keep tree species and waterlessness.
verses.before: For you will be as an oak whose leaf fades, and as a garden that has no water.
verses.after: You will be like a terebinth with withering leaves, like a garden without water.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you will be as an oak whose leaf fades, and as a garden that has no water.

verses.rationale: Retain worker/work linkage and unquenched fire.
verses.before: The strong will be like tinder, and his work like a spark. They will both burn together, and no one will quench them."
verses.after: The strong will become tinder, and their work a spark. Both will burn together, with no one to put them out.
verses.tsw_comparator: The strong will be like tinder, and his work like a spark. They will both burn together, and no one will quench them."

verses.rationale: Preserve unusual seeing a word formula.
verses.before: This is what Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.after: The word Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem:
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keep raised mountain and uphill flowing nations.
verses.before: It will happen in the latter days, that the mountain of the LORD's house will be established on the top of the mountains, and will be raised above the hills; and all nations will flow to it.
verses.after: In days to come, the mountain of the **LORD**’s house will stand firm above the mountains, raised above the hills. All nations will stream toward it.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen in the latter days, that the mountain of the LORD's house will be established on the top of the mountains, and will be raised above the hills; and all nations will flow to it.

verses.rationale: Retain collective invitation and learning/walking relation.
verses.before: Many peoples will go and say, "Come, let's go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths." For out of Zion the law will go forth, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
verses.after: Many peoples will come and say, “Come, let us go up to the **LORD**’s mountain, to the house of Jacob’s God. He will teach us his ways, and we will walk his paths.” For instruction will go out from Zion, and the **LORD**’s word from Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many peoples will go and say, "Come, let's go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths." For out of Zion the law will go forth, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserve instruments transformed and unlearned warfare.
verses.before: The LORD will judge between the nations and decide matters for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will not learn war any more.
verses.after: He will judge between the nations and settle disputes for many peoples. They will hammer their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift sword against nation; they will no longer learn war.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will judge between the nations and decide matters for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will not learn war any more.

verses.rationale: Retain invitation echo and light image.
verses.before: House of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of the LORD.
verses.after: House of Jacob, come! Let us walk in the **LORD**’s light.
verses.tsw_comparator: House of Jacob, come, and let us walk in the light of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain address to God and difficult foreign practice claims.
verses.before: For you have forsaken your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled from the east, with people who practice divination like the Philistines, and they clasp hands with the children of foreigners.
verses.after: You have abandoned your people, the house of Jacob. They are full of practices from the east, of diviners like the Philistines; they clasp hands with foreigners.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have forsaken your people, the house of Jacob, because they are filled from the east, with those who practice divination like the Philistines, and they clasp hands with the children of foreigners.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated fullness and endlessness.
verses.before: Their land is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures. Their land also is full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots.
verses.after: Their land is full of silver and gold, with no end to their treasures; their land is full of horses, with no end to their chariots.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their land is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures. Their land also is full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots.

verses.rationale: Preserve hand/finger irony.
verses.before: Their land also is full of idols. They worship the work of their own hands, what their own fingers have made.
verses.after: Their land is full of idols. They bow to the work of their hands, to what their own fingers have made.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their land also is full of idols. They worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made.

verses.rationale: Retain startling negative petition.
verses.before: Man is brought low, and humanity is humbled; so do not forgive them.
verses.after: Humanity bows down; people are brought low. Do not forgive them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Man is brought low, and humanity is humbled; therefore do not forgive them.

verses.rationale: Keep hiding command and paired divine effects.
verses.before: Enter into the rock, and hide in the dust, from before the terror of the LORD, and from the glory of his majesty.
verses.after: Go into the rocks; hide in the dust from the terror of the **LORD**, from the splendor of his majesty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Enter into the rock, and hide in the dust, from before the terror of the LORD, and from the glory of his majesty.

verses.rationale: Preserve human/divine height reversal.
verses.before: The lofty looks of man will be brought low, the haughtiness of men will be bowed down, and the LORD alone will be exalted on that day.
verses.after: Humanity’s proud eyes will be lowered; human arrogance will bow. The **LORD** alone will be exalted on that day.
verses.tsw_comparator: The lofty looks of man will be brought low, the haughtiness of men will be bowed down, and the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.

verses.rationale: Retain day against exalted things and continuation.
verses.before: For there will be a day of the LORD of Hosts for all that is proud and haughty, and for all that is lifted up; and it will be brought low:
verses.after: For the **LORD** of hosts has a day against everything proud and lofty, everything raised high—it will be brought low;
verses.tsw_comparator: For there will be a day of the LORD of Hosts for all that is proud and haughty, and for all that is lifted up; and it will be brought low:

verses.rationale: Keep two named tree regions.
verses.before: For all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, for all the oaks of Bashan,
verses.after: against all Lebanon’s cedars, tall and towering, and all Bashan’s oaks;
verses.tsw_comparator: For all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, for all the oaks of Bashan,

verses.rationale: Preserve mountain/hill parallel.
verses.before: For all the high mountains, for all the hills that are lifted up,
verses.after: against all the high mountains and every towering hill;
verses.tsw_comparator: For all the high mountains, for all the hills that are lifted up,

verses.rationale: Retain military architecture.
verses.before: For every lofty tower, for every fortified wall,
verses.after: against every lofty tower and every fortified wall;
verses.tsw_comparator: For every lofty tower, for every fortified wall,

verses.rationale: Keep Tarshish ships, uncertain second noun noted.
verses.before: For all the ships of Tarshish, and for all pleasant imagery.
verses.after: against all the ships of Tarshish and every splendid vessel.
verses.tsw_comparator: For all the ships of Tarshish, and for all pleasant imagery.

verses.rationale: Match refrain with source’s altered order.
verses.before: The loftiness of man will be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men will be brought low; and the LORD alone will be exalted on that day.
verses.after: Human arrogance will bow; humanity’s pride will be lowered. The **LORD** alone will be exalted on that day.
verses.tsw_comparator: The loftiness of man will be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men will be brought low; and the LORD alone will be exalted in that day.

verses.rationale: Retain total disappearance.
verses.before: The idols will utterly pass away.
verses.after: The idols will disappear completely.
verses.tsw_comparator: The idols will utterly pass away.

verses.rationale: Keep expanded hiding refrain and earth terror.
verses.before: Men will go into the caves of the rocks, and into the holes of the earth, from before the terror of the LORD, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.
verses.after: People will enter caves in the rocks and holes in the earth, from the terror of the **LORD**, from the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to make the earth tremble.
verses.tsw_comparator: Men will go into the caves of the rocks, and into the holes of the earth, from before the terror of the LORD, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.

verses.rationale: Retain metals, animals, and unfinished action.
verses.before: On that day, men will cast away their idols of silver, and their idols of gold, which have been made for themselves to worship, to the moles and to the bats;
verses.after: On that day people will throw away the silver idols and gold idols made for them to worship— throw them to the moles and bats—
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day, men will cast away their idols of silver, and their idols of gold, which have been made for themselves to worship, to the moles and to the bats;

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated refrain and rock variations.
verses.before: To go into the caverns of the rocks, and into the clefts of the ragged rocks, from before the terror of the LORD, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.
verses.after: to enter clefts in the rocks and cracks in the cliffs, from the terror of the **LORD**, from the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to make the earth tremble.
verses.tsw_comparator: To go into the caverns of the rocks, and into the clefts of the ragged rocks, from before the terror of the LORD, and from the glory of his majesty, when he arises to shake the earth mightily.

verses.rationale: Retain mortal breath and valuation question.
verses.before: Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for of what account is he?
verses.after: Stop relying on human beings, whose breath is in their nostrils. What are they worth?
verses.tsw_comparator: Stop trusting in man, whose breath is in his nostrils; for of what account is he?

verses.rationale: Preserve divine titles and repeated support.
verses.before: For, look, the Lord GOD of Hosts, takes away from Jerusalem and from Judah supply and support, the whole supply of bread, and the whole supply of water;
verses.after: Look! The Lord, the **LORD** of hosts, is removing from Jerusalem and Judah every support and supply: all support of bread and water,
verses.tsw_comparator: For, look, the Lord GOD of Hosts, takes away from Jerusalem and from Judah supply and support, the whole supply of bread, and the whole supply of water;

verses.rationale: Retain all six social roles.
verses.before: the mighty man, the man of war, the judge, the prophet, the diviner, the elder,
verses.after: warrior and soldier, judge and prophet, diviner and elder,
verses.tsw_comparator: the mighty man, the man of war, the judge, the prophet, the diviner, the elder,

verses.rationale: Keep fifty and ambiguous skilled professions.
verses.before: the captain of fifty, the honorable man, the counselor, the skilled craftsman, and the clever enchanter.
verses.after: captain of fifty and person of rank, counselor, skilled craftsman, and expert in charms.
verses.tsw_comparator: the captain of fifty, the honorable man, the counselor, the skilled craftsman, and the clever enchanter.

verses.rationale: Retain divine appointment and instability image.
verses.before: I will give boys to be their princes, and children will rule over them.
verses.after: “I will make boys their rulers; capricious children will govern them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give boys to be their princes, and children will rule over them.

verses.rationale: Keep mutual harm and age/status reversals.
verses.before: The people will be oppressed, everyone by another, and everyone by his neighbor. The child will behave himself proudly against the old man, and the base against the honorable.
verses.after: People will oppress one another, each against a neighbor. The young will bully the old, the despised the honored.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people will be oppressed, everyone by another, and everyone by his neighbor. The child will behave himself proudly against the old man, and the base against the honorable.

verses.rationale: Retain kin setting and absurd cloak qualification.
verses.before: Indeed a man will take hold of his brother in the house of his father, saying, "You have clothing, you be our ruler, and let this ruin be under your hand."
verses.after: A man will seize his brother in their father’s house: “You have a cloak—be our leader! Take charge of this heap of ruins.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Indeed a man will take hold of his brother in the house of his father, saying, "You have clothing, you be our ruler, and let this ruin be under your hand."

verses.rationale: Keep healer metaphor and refused office.
verses.before: On that day he will cry out, saying, I will not be a healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing. You will not make me ruler of the people.
verses.after: But that day he will protest: “I cannot bind up your wounds! My house has neither bread nor cloak. Do not make me the people’s leader.”
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day he will cry out, saying, I will not be a healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing. You will not make me ruler of the people.

verses.rationale: Render eyes of glory as presence with note.
verses.before: For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen; because their tongue and their doings are against the LORD, to provoke the eyes of his glory.
verses.after: Jerusalem has stumbled; Judah has fallen. Their speech and deeds oppose the **LORD**, defying his glorious presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen; because their tongue and their doings are against the LORD, to provoke the eyes of his glory.

verses.rationale: Retain self-incrimination and explicit Sodom.
verses.before: The look of their faces testify against them. They parade their sin like Sodom. They do not hide it. Woe to their soul! For they have brought disaster upon themselves.
verses.after: Their faces testify against them; like Sodom, they declare their sin without hiding it. Woe to them! They have brought harm on themselves.
verses.tsw_comparator: The look of their faces testify against them. They parade their sin like Sodom. They do not hide it. Woe to their soul! For they have brought disaster upon themselves.

verses.rationale: Keep eating moral fruit.
verses.before: Tell the righteous "Good!" For they will eat the fruit of their deeds.
verses.after: Tell the righteous it will go well: they will eat the fruit of their deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tell the righteous "Good!" For they will eat the fruit of their deeds.

verses.rationale: Retain recompense and hands.
verses.before: Woe to the wicked! Disaster is upon them; for the deeds of his hands will be paid back to him.
verses.after: Woe to the wicked! It will go badly: what their hands have done will return to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to the wicked! Disaster is upon them; for the deeds of his hands will be paid back to him.

verses.rationale: Preserve gendered indictment, no silent alternate vocalization.
verses.before: As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. My people, people who lead you cause you to err, and destroy the way of your paths.
verses.after: My people—children oppress them, and women rule over them. My people, your guides mislead you; they swallow up the path you should walk.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. My people, those who lead you cause you to err, and destroy the way of your paths.

verses.rationale: Keep courtroom and plural peoples.
verses.before: The LORD stands up to contend, and stands to judge the peoples.
verses.after: The **LORD** takes his stand to argue the case; he rises to judge peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD stands up to contend, and stands to judge the peoples.

verses.rationale: Retain vineyard accusation and concrete stolen goods.
verses.before: The LORD will enter into judgment with the elders of his people, and their leaders: "It is you who have eaten up the vineyard. The spoil of the poor is in your houses.
verses.after: The **LORD** enters judgment with his people’s elders and rulers: “You have devoured the vineyard! Your houses hold what you stole from the poor.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will enter into judgment with the elders of his people, and their leaders: "It is you who have eaten up the vineyard. The spoil of the poor is in your houses.

verses.rationale: Keep physical violence and divine-name typography distinction.
verses.before: What do you mean that you crush my people, and grind the face of the poor?" says the Lord GOD of Hosts.
verses.after: What do you mean by crushing my people, grinding the faces of the poor?” declares the Lord **GOD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: What do you mean that you crush my people, and grind the face of the poor?" says the Lord GOD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retain specific female display and causal continuation.
verses.before: Moreover the LORD said, "Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with outstretched necks and flirting eyes, walking to trip as they go, jingling ornaments on their feet;
verses.after: The **LORD** says: “Because Zion’s daughters are proud, walking with necks outstretched and eyes that flirt, taking mincing steps and jingling their anklets,
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover the LORD said, "Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with outstretched necks and flirting eyes, walking to trip as they go, jingling ornaments on their feet;

verses.rationale: Preserve humiliating bodily threat, alternative scalp noted.
verses.before: so the Lord brings sores on the crown of the head of the women of Zion, and the LORD will make their scalps bald."
verses.after: the Lord will scab the heads of Zion’s daughters; the **LORD** will expose their private parts.”
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore the Lord brings sores on the crown of the head of the women of Zion, and the LORD will make their scalps bald."

verses.rationale: Retain complete adornment catalogue beginning.
verses.before: On that day the Lord will take away the beauty of their anklets, the headbands, the crescent necklaces,
verses.after: On that day the Lord will remove their finery: anklets, headbands, crescent ornaments,
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day the Lord will take away the beauty of their anklets, the headbands, the crescent necklaces,

verses.rationale: Preserve three ornaments without expansion.
verses.before: the earrings, the bracelets, the veils,
verses.after: earrings, bracelets, veils,
verses.tsw_comparator: the earrings, the bracelets, the veils,

verses.rationale: Keep five distinct items and magical ornament.
verses.before: the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume bottles, the charms,
verses.after: headdresses, ankle chains, sashes, perfume containers, amulets,
verses.tsw_comparator: the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume bottles, the charms,

verses.rationale: Retain two jewelry locations.
verses.before: the signet rings, the nose rings,
verses.after: rings and nose jewels,
verses.tsw_comparator: the signet rings, the nose rings,

verses.rationale: Keep four garment/accessory terms.
verses.before: the fine robes, the capes, the cloaks, the purses,
verses.after: fine robes, mantles, wraps, purses,
verses.tsw_comparator: the fine robes, the capes, the cloaks, the purses,

verses.rationale: Preserve final four items, uncertain identifications noted.
verses.before: the hand mirrors, the fine linen garments, the tiaras, and the shawls.
verses.after: mirrors, linen garments, turbans, and shawls.
verses.tsw_comparator: the hand mirrors, the fine linen garments, the tiaras, and the shawls.

verses.rationale: Keep five humiliating exchanges.
verses.before: It will happen that instead of sweet spices, there will be rottenness; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of well set hair, baldness; instead of a robe, a girding of sackcloth; and branding instead of beauty.
verses.after: Instead of perfume, rot; instead of a sash, a rope; instead of styled hair, baldness; instead of a fine robe, sackcloth; branding instead of beauty.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen that instead of sweet spices, there will be rottenness; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of well set hair, baldness; instead of a robe, a girding of sackcloth; and branding instead of beauty.

verses.rationale: Retain address to city and deaths.
verses.before: Your men will fall by the sword, and your mighty in the war.
verses.after: Your men will fall by the sword, your warriors in battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your men will fall by the sword, and your mighty in the war.

verses.rationale: Preserve personified gates and devastated woman-city.
verses.before: Her gates will lament and mourn; and she will be desolate and sit on the ground.
verses.after: Her gates will lament and mourn; stripped bare, she will sit on the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her gates will lament and mourn; and she will be desolate and sit on the ground.

verses.rationale: Keep seven-to-one ratio and women’s stated proposal.
verses.before: Seven women will take hold of one man on that day, saying, "We will eat our own bread, and wear our own clothing: only let us be called by your name. Take away our reproach."
verses.after: On that day seven women will seize one man and say, “We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes. Only let us bear your name; take away our disgrace.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Seven women will take hold of one man in that day, saying, "We will eat our own bread, and wear our own clothing: only let us be called by your name. Take away our reproach."

verses.rationale: Keep plant/fruit parallel, branch alternative noted.
verses.before: On that day, the LORD's branch will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the beauty and glory of the survivors of Israel.
verses.after: On that day the **LORD**’s growth will be beautiful and glorious, and the land’s fruit will be the pride and splendor of Israel’s survivors.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day, the LORD's branch will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the beauty and glory of the survivors of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retain remnant and life register.
verses.before: It will happen, that the one who is left in Zion, and the one who remains in Jerusalem, will be called holy, even everyone who is written among the living in Jerusalem;
verses.after: Those left in Zion, those remaining in Jerusalem, will be called holy—everyone recorded for life in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen, that the one who is left in Zion, and the one who remains in Jerusalem, will be called holy, even everyone who is written among the living in Jerusalem;

verses.rationale: Preserve washing, blood, and spirit ambiguity.
verses.before: when the Lord will have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and will have purged the blood of Jerusalem from its midst, by the spirit of justice, and by the spirit of burning.
verses.after: When the Lord has washed away the filth of Zion’s daughters and rinsed Jerusalem’s blood from her midst by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning,
verses.tsw_comparator: when the Lord will have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and will have purged the blood of Jerusalem from its midst, by the spirit of justice, and by the spirit of burning.

verses.rationale: Keep cloud/fire pattern and covering.
verses.before: The LORD will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion, and over her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory will be a canopy.
verses.after: the **LORD** will create over all Mount Zion’s dwelling places and assemblies a cloud by day, smoke, and the glow of flaming fire by night. Over all the glory there will be a canopy,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will create over the whole habitation of Mount Zion, and over her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night; for over all the glory will be a canopy.

verses.rationale: Retain weather-specific protection.
verses.before: There will be a pavilion for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for a refuge and for a shelter from storm and from rain.
verses.after: a shelter giving shade from the daytime heat, a refuge and hiding place from storm and rain.
verses.tsw_comparator: There will be a pavilion for a shade in the daytime from the heat, and for a refuge and for a shelter from storm and from rain.

verses.rationale: Keep singer and beloved distinct.
verses.before: Let me sing for my beloved my beloved’s song concerning his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hill.
verses.after: Let me sing for my beloved my beloved’s song about his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hillside.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let me sing for my beloved my beloved’s song concerning his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hill.

verses.rationale: Preserve preparations and failed expectation.
verses.before: He dug it and cleared it of stones, and planted it with choice vines. He built a tower among it, and also carved out a wine vat in it. He waited for it to yield grapes, but it produced wild grapes.
verses.after: He dug it, cleared its stones, and planted choice vines. He built a tower in its midst and cut out a winepress. He expected grapes, but it produced foul fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: He dug it and cleared it of stones, and planted it with choice vines. He built a tower in the midst of it, and also carved out a wine vat in it. He waited for it to yield grapes, but it produced wild grapes.

verses.rationale: Keep owner’s first-person appeal.
verses.before: So now, inhabitants of Jerusalem and people of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
verses.after: “Now, inhabitants of Jerusalem and people of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
verses.tsw_comparator: So now, inhabitants of Jerusalem and people of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated fruit question.
verses.before: What more was there to do for my vineyard that I have not done in it? Why, when I waited for grapes, did it yield wild grapes?
verses.after: What more could I have done for my vineyard that I have not done? Why, when I expected grapes, did it produce foul fruit?
verses.tsw_comparator: What more was there to do for my vineyard that I have not done in it? Why, when I waited for grapes, did it yield wild grapes?

verses.rationale: Keep two removed protections and consequences.
verses.before: Now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard. I will remove its hedge, and it will become waste; I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled.
verses.after: Now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: remove its hedge, and it will be devoured; break its wall, and it will be trampled.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard. I will remove its hedge, and it will become waste; I will break down its wall, and it shall be trampled.

verses.rationale: Retain agricultural neglect and cloud command.
verses.before: I will make it a desolation; it will not be pruned nor hoed, and briars and thorns will grow; I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.
verses.after: I will make it a wasteland, neither pruned nor hoed, overgrown with thorns and briers. I will command the clouds to send no rain on it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make it a desolation; it will not be pruned nor hoed, and briars and thorns shall grow; I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.

verses.rationale: Preserve accusation’s sound-driven contrasts in note.
verses.before: For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are his pleasant planting; he waited for justice, but look, bloodshed; for righteousness, but look, an outcry!
verses.after: The vineyard of the **LORD** of hosts is the house of Israel; the people of Judah are the planting he delighted in. He expected justice—but look, bloodshed! Righteousness—but listen, a cry!
verses.tsw_comparator: For the vineyard of the LORD of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are his pleasant planting; he waited for justice, but behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, but behold, an outcry!

verses.rationale: Keep land concentration and exclusion.
verses.before: Woe to people who join house to house, who add field to field, until there is no place left, and you are left alone in the land.
verses.after: Woe to those who join house to house and add field to field, until no room remains and you live alone in the land!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to those who join house to house, who add field to field, until there is no place left, and you are left alone in the land.

verses.rationale: Supply speech for in-my-ears formula.
verses.before: In my hearing, the LORD of Hosts said: Surely many houses will be desolate, large and beautiful, without inhabitant.
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts has spoken in my hearing: “Surely many houses will lie desolate, large and beautiful, with no one living there.
verses.tsw_comparator: In my hearing, the LORD of Hosts said: Surely many houses shall be desolate, large and beautiful, without inhabitant.

verses.rationale: Preserve exact ancient quantities for note.
verses.before: For ten acres of vineyard will produce but one bath, and a homer of seed will yield but an ephah.
verses.after: Ten yoke of vineyard will yield one bath, and a homer of seed will yield an ephah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For ten acres of vineyard shall produce but one bath, and a homer of seed shall yield but an ephah.

verses.rationale: Keep morning/night and burning wine.
verses.before: Woe to people who rise early in the morning that they may run after strong drink, who tarry late into the evening as wine inflames them!
verses.after: Woe to those who rise early to chase strong drink and linger late, inflamed by wine!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to those who rise early in the morning that they may run after strong drink, who tarry late into the evening as wine inflames them!

verses.rationale: Retain four instruments and ignored divine work.
verses.before: They have lyre and harp, tambourine and flute, and wine at their feasts, but they do not regard the deeds of the LORD, or see the work of his hands.
verses.after: Lyre and harp, tambourine and flute, and wine fill their feasts. But they do not regard the **LORD**’s work or see what his hands have done.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have lyre and harp, tambourine and flute, and wine at their feasts, but they do not regard the deeds of the LORD, or see the work of his hands.

verses.rationale: Keep exile, status contrast, hunger/thirst.
verses.before: So my people go into exile for lack of knowledge; their honored men go hungry, and their multitude parched with thirst.
verses.after: So my people go into exile for lack of knowledge. Their honored people die of hunger; their masses are parched with thirst.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore my people go into exile for lack of knowledge; their honored men go hungry, and their multitude parched with thirst.

verses.rationale: Preserve devouring underworld and descent.
verses.before: So Sheol enlarges its appetite and opens its mouth beyond measure; and down go her nobles, and her masses, her revelers, and people who exult in her.
verses.after: So Sheol widens its appetite and opens its mouth without limit. Down go Jerusalem’s splendor and crowds, her uproar and revelers.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore Sheol enlarges its appetite and opens its mouth beyond measure; and down go her nobles, and her masses, her revelers, and those who exult in her.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated lowering and eyes.
verses.before: The people are bowed down, everyone brought low; and the eyes of the haughty are humbled.
verses.after: Humanity bows down; people are brought low; proud eyes are lowered.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people are bowed down, everyone brought low; and the eyes of the haughty are humbled.

verses.rationale: Keep holiness/justice linkage.
verses.before: But the LORD of Hosts is exalted in justice, and the Holy God shows himself holy in righteousness.
verses.after: But the **LORD** of hosts is exalted through justice; the holy God shows himself holy through righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD of Hosts is exalted in justice, and the Holy God shows himself holy in righteousness.

verses.rationale: Follow strangers text, not silently lambs emendation.
verses.before: Then will the lambs graze as in their pasture, and nomads will eat among the ruins of the rich.
verses.after: Lambs will graze as in their pasture, and strangers will eat among the ruins of the well-fed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then shall the lambs graze as in their pasture, and nomads shall eat among the ruins of the rich.

verses.rationale: Keep hauling metaphor and differing ropes.
verses.before: Woe to people who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, who draw sin as with cart ropes,
verses.after: Woe to those who drag guilt with cords of falsehood and sin as with cart ropes,
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of falsehood, who draw sin as with cart ropes,

verses.rationale: Preserve mocking demand and title.
verses.before: who say, “Let him make haste, let him speed his work that we may see it; let the purpose of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it!”
verses.after: who say, “Let him hurry! Let him speed his work so we can see it! Let the Holy One of Israel’s plan come near, let it arrive so we may know!”
verses.tsw_comparator: who say, “Let him make haste, let him speed his work that we may see it; let the purpose of the Holy One of Israel draw near and come, that we may know it!”

verses.rationale: Keep three reversible pairs.
verses.before: Woe to people who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter!
verses.after: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness into light and light into darkness, who turn bitter into sweet and sweet into bitter!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter!

verses.rationale: Retain self-assessed wisdom.
verses.before: Woe to people who are wise in their own eyes, and shrewd in their own sight!
verses.after: Woe to those wise in their own eyes and discerning in their own sight!
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, and shrewd in their own sight!

verses.rationale: Keep ironic military praise.
verses.before: Woe to people who are heroes at drinking wine, and valiant men in mixing strong drink,
verses.after: Woe to heroes at drinking wine, valiant men at mixing strong drink,
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine, and valiant men in mixing strong drink,

verses.rationale: Retain courtroom injustice.
verses.before: who acquit the guilty for a bribe, and deprive the innocent of his right!
verses.after: who acquit the wicked for a bribe and take the righteous person’s rights away!
verses.tsw_comparator: who acquit the guilty for a bribe, and deprive the innocent of his right!

verses.rationale: Keep two combustion images and root/blossom destruction.
verses.before: So, as the tongue of fire devours stubble, and as dry grass sinks down in flame, so their root will be as rottenness, and their blossom go up like dust; for they have rejected the law of the LORD of Hosts, and have despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: As a tongue of fire eats stubble and dry grass collapses in flame, their root will rot and their blossom rise like dust. They have rejected the instruction of the **LORD** of hosts and scorned the Holy One of Israel’s word.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, as the tongue of fire devours stubble, and as dry grass sinks down in flame, so their root will be as rottenness, and their blossom go up like dust; for they have rejected the law of the LORD of Hosts, and have despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserve bodies and recurring anger refrain.
verses.before: So the anger of the LORD was kindled against his people, and he stretched out his hand against them and struck them, and the mountains quaked; and their corpses were as refuse in the streets. For all this his anger has not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.
verses.after: So the **LORD**’s anger burned against his people. He stretched out his hand and struck them; mountains shook, and their corpses lay like refuse in the streets. For all this, his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the anger of the LORD was kindled against his people, and he stretched out his hand against them and struck them, and the mountains quaked; and their corpses were as refuse in the streets. For all this his anger has not turned away, and his hand is stretched out still.

verses.rationale: Keep plural/singular collective movement and summons.
verses.before: He will raise a signal for nations far away, and whistle for them from the end of the earth; And look, they quickly come,
verses.after: He will raise a signal for distant nations and whistle for them from the earth’s end. Look, they come swiftly, speedily!
verses.tsw_comparator: He will raise a signal for nations far away, and whistle for them from the end of the earth; And behold, they quickly come,

verses.rationale: Retain four readiness negatives.
verses.before: none is weary, none stumbles, none slumbers or sleeps, not a belt is loose, nor a sandal strap broken;
verses.after: None grows tired or stumbles; none dozes or sleeps. No belt at the waist comes loose; no sandal strap breaks.
verses.tsw_comparator: none is weary, none stumbles, none slumbers or sleeps, not a belt is loose, nor a sandal strap broken;

verses.rationale: Keep weapon and chariot similes.
verses.before: their arrows are sharp, all their bows bent, Their horses' hooves seem like flint, And their wheels like the whirlwind.
verses.after: Their arrows are sharp, all their bows drawn. Their horses’ hooves seem like flint, their wheels like a whirlwind.
verses.tsw_comparator: their arrows are sharp, all their bows bent, Their horses' hooves seem like flint, And their wheels like the whirlwind.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated lion sounds and absent rescue.
verses.before: Their roaring is like a lioness; like young lions they roar, they growl and seize their prey; they carry it off, and none can rescue.
verses.after: Their roar is like a lion’s; they roar like young lions. They growl, seize prey, and carry it off with no one to rescue it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their roaring is like a lioness; like young lions they roar, they growl and seize their prey; they carry it off, and none can rescue.

verses.rationale: Preserve ominous land view and darkened light.
verses.before: They will growl over it on that day, like the roaring of the sea. And if one looks to the land— look, darkness and distress; and the light is darkened by its clouds.
verses.after: On that day they will growl over it like the sea’s roar. Look toward the land: darkness and distress! Even the light is darkened by its clouds.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will growl over it on that day, like the roaring of the sea. And if one looks to the land— behold, darkness and distress; and the light is darkened by its clouds.

verses.rationale: Retain dated vision and robe scale.
verses.before: In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.
verses.after: In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up. The train of his robe filled the temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.

verses.rationale: Keep six divided into three pairs.
verses.before: Above him stood the seraphim. Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew.
verses.after: Seraphim stood above him. Each had six wings: with two each covered his face, with two his feet, and with two he flew.
verses.tsw_comparator: Above him stood the seraphim. Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew.

verses.rationale: Preserve threefold holy and antiphonal call.
verses.before: And one called to another and said, “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; the entire earth is full of the LORD’s glory.”
verses.after: They called to one another: “Holy, holy, holy is the **LORD** of hosts! The whole earth is full of his glory!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And one called to another and said, “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; the whole earth is full of the LORD’s glory.”

verses.rationale: Retain structural shaking and smoke.
verses.before: The foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of the one who called, and the house was filled with smoke.
verses.after: The doorposts shook at the sound of the one calling, and the house filled with smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: The foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of the one who called, and the house was filled with smoke.

verses.rationale: Keep shared impurity and royal vision.
verses.before: Then I said, "Woe is me! For I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips: for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts!"
verses.after: I said, “Woe to me! I am undone. I am a man of unclean lips, living among a people of unclean lips, yet my eyes have seen the King, the **LORD** of hosts.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, "Woe is me! For I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts!"

verses.rationale: Retain altar and tool-mediated coal.
verses.before: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.
verses.after: One of the seraphim flew to me with a glowing coal in his hand, taken from the altar with tongs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserve physical contact and atonement term.
verses.before: He touched my mouth with it, and said, "Look, this has touched your lips; and your iniquity is taken away, and your sin forgiven."
verses.after: He touched my mouth and said, “Look, this has touched your lips. Your guilt has departed; your sin is atoned for.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He touched my mouth with it, and said, "Look, this has touched your lips; and your iniquity is taken away, and your sin forgiven."

verses.rationale: Keep singular/plural divine speech unharmonized.

verses.rationale: Preserve child/son, shoulder, full titles without extra doctrinal gloss.
verses.before: For a child has been born to us, a son has been given to us; authority rests upon his shoulder, and his name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
verses.after: For a child has been born for us, a son has been given to us. Authority rests on his shoulder, and his name is called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a child has been born to us, a son has been given to us; authority rests upon his shoulder, and his name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

verses.rationale: Keep rule, Davidic throne, justice, and divine zeal.
verses.before: Of the increase of his authority and of peace there will be no end, upon the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and uphold it with justice and righteousness from now and for ever. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will do this.
verses.after: His authority will increase, and peace will have no end, on David’s throne and over his kingdom, establishing and upholding it with justice and righteousness from now and forever. The zeal of the **LORD** of hosts will do this.
verses.tsw_comparator: Of the increase of his authority and of peace there will be no end, upon the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and uphold it with justice and righteousness from now and for ever. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will do this.

verses.rationale: Retain word as active falling agent.
verses.before: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel.
verses.after: The Lord sent a word against Jacob; it fell upon Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it falls on Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep named audience and coming quotation.
verses.before: All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and in arrogance of heart,
verses.after: All the people will know it— Ephraim and Samaria’s inhabitants, who say in pride and arrogance,
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people will know, including Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, who say in pride and in arrogance of heart,

verses.rationale: Preserve two boasts of upgraded materials.
verses.before: "The bricks have fallen, but we will build with hewn stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place."
verses.after: “Bricks have fallen, but we will build with cut stone. Sycamores have been felled, but we will replace them with cedars.”
verses.tsw_comparator: "The bricks have fallen, but we will build with hewn stone. The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place."

verses.rationale: Retain Rezin’s adversaries rather than emend name.
verses.before: So the LORD will set up on high against him the adversaries of Rezin, and will stir up his enemies,
verses.after: The **LORD** raised Rezin’s adversaries against them and stirred up their enemies:
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the LORD will set up on high against him the adversaries of Rezin, and will stir up his enemies,

verses.rationale: Keep directions and recurring anger refrain.
verses.before: The Syrians in front, and the Philistines behind; and they will devour Israel with open mouth. For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.after: Aram from the east, Philistines from the west, devouring Israel with open mouths. For all this, his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Syrians in front, and the Philistines behind; and they will devour Israel with open mouth. For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

verses.rationale: Retain failure to return and seek.
verses.before: Yet the people have not turned to the one who struck them, neither have they sought the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: The people did not return to the one who struck them; they did not seek the **LORD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet the people have not turned to the one who struck them, neither have they sought the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keep paired extremes and one day.
verses.before: So the LORD will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in one day.
verses.after: So the **LORD** cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in a single day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the LORD will cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in one day.

verses.rationale: Preserve text’s own decoding of metaphor.
verses.before: The elder and the honorable man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
verses.after: The elder and person of rank are the head; the prophet teaching lies is the tail.
verses.tsw_comparator: The elder and the honorable man is the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.

verses.rationale: Keep guide repetition and devouring verb.
verses.before: For people who lead this people lead them astray; and people who are led by them are destroyed.
verses.after: This people’s guides mislead them; those they guide are swallowed up.
verses.tsw_comparator: For those who lead this people lead them astray; and those who are led by them are destroyed.

verses.rationale: Preserve disturbing withheld compassion and exact refrain.
verses.before: So the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, neither will he have compassion on their orphan and widows; for everyone is profane and an evil-doer, and every mouth speaks folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.after: Therefore the Lord takes no pleasure in their young men and has no compassion on their fatherless or widows, for everyone is godless and does evil; every mouth speaks folly. For all this, his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over their young men, neither will he have compassion on their orphan and widows; for everyone is profane and an evil-doer, and every mouth speaks folly. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

verses.rationale: Keep evil as spreading fire.
verses.before: For wickedness burns like a fire. It devours the briers and thorns; yes, it kindles in the thickets of the forest, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.
verses.after: Wickedness burns like fire; it eats thorns and briers, sets the forest thickets ablaze, and they roll upward in columns of smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: For wickedness burns like a fire. It devours the briers and thorns; yes, it kindles in the thickets of the forest, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.

verses.rationale: Retain divine wrath and failed kin compassion.
verses.before: Through the wrath of the LORD of Hosts, the land is burnt up; and the people are the fuel for the fire. No one spares his brother.
verses.after: By the **LORD** of hosts’ wrath the land is scorched; the people become fuel for fire. No one spares a brother.
verses.tsw_comparator: Through the wrath of the LORD of Hosts, the land is burnt up; and the people are the fuel for the fire. No one spares his brother.

verses.rationale: Follow arm text, preserve cannibalistic metaphor.
verses.before: One will devour on the right hand, and be hungry; and he will eat on the left hand, and they will not be satisfied. Everyone will eat the flesh of his own arm:
verses.after: They snatch on the right and remain hungry, eat on the left and are not satisfied. Each devours the flesh of his own arm:
verses.tsw_comparator: One will devour on the right hand, and be hungry; and he will eat on the left hand, and they will not be satisfied. Everyone will eat the flesh of his own arm:

verses.rationale: Keep intra-Israel conflict and repeated refrain.
verses.before: Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh; and they together will be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.after: Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they turn against Judah. For all this, his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh; and they together will be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

verses.rationale: Retain written injustice and repeated decree.
verses.before: Woe to people who decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers who write oppressive decrees;
verses.after: Woe to those who decree unjust decrees, to scribes who keep writing oppression,
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, and to the writers who write oppressive decrees;

verses.rationale: Preserve four legal and predatory harms.
verses.before: to deprive the needy from justice, and to rob the poor among my people of their rights, that widows may be their spoil, and that they may make the orphan their prey!
verses.after: to deny the poor a hearing and rob my afflicted people of justice, making widows their plunder and the fatherless their prey!
verses.tsw_comparator: to deprive the needy from justice, and to rob the poor among my people of their rights, that widows may be their spoil, and that they may make the orphan their prey!

verses.rationale: Keep three unanswered judgment questions.
verses.before: What will you do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which will come from afar? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?
verses.after: What will you do on the day of reckoning, when devastation comes from far away? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?
verses.tsw_comparator: What will you do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which will come from afar? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?

verses.rationale: Retain two fates and established refrain.
verses.before: They will only bow down under the prisoners, and will fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
verses.after: Nothing remains but to crouch among prisoners or fall among the slain. For all this, his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will only bow down under the prisoners, and will fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

verses.rationale: Keep instrument metaphor and divine anger.
verses.before: Alas Assyrian, the rod of my anger, the staff in whose hand is my indignation!
verses.after: “Woe to Assyria, the rod of my anger! The staff in their hand is my fury.
verses.tsw_comparator: Alas Assyrian, the rod of my anger, the staff in whose hand is my indignation!

verses.rationale: Retain divine commissioning and paired spoil verbs.
verses.before: I will send him against a profane nation, and against the people who anger me will I give him a charge to take the spoil and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.
verses.after: I send him against a godless nation; I command him against the people of my wrath, to take spoil and seize plunder, to trample them like street mud.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will send him against a profane nation, and against the people who anger me will I give him a charge to take the spoil and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.

verses.rationale: Distinguish instrument’s intention from sender’s.
verses.before: However he does not mean so, neither does his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy, and to cut off not a few nations.
verses.after: But that is not what he intends; that is not what his heart plans. His heart is set on destruction, on cutting off nations without number.
verses.tsw_comparator: However he does not mean so, neither does his heart think so; but it is in his heart to destroy, and to cut off not a few nations.

verses.rationale: Keep boast as Assyrian speech.
verses.before: For he says, "Aren't all of my princes kings?
verses.after: He says, ‘Are not all my commanders kings?
verses.tsw_comparator: For he says, "Aren't all of my princes kings?

verses.rationale: Preserve six cities and paired comparisons.
verses.before: Isn't Calno like Carchemish? Isn't Hamath like Arpad? Isn't Samaria like Damascus?"
verses.after: Is not Calno like Carchemish, Hamath like Arpad, Samaria like Damascus?
verses.tsw_comparator: Isn't Calno like Carchemish? Isn't Hamath like Arpad? Isn't Samaria like Damascus?"

verses.rationale: Keep speaker’s comparative religious boast.
verses.before: As my hand has found the kingdoms of the idols, whose engraved images exceeded those of Jerusalem and of Samaria;
verses.after: My hand has reached kingdoms of idols whose images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria.
verses.tsw_comparator: As my hand has found the kingdoms of the idols, whose engraved images exceeded those of Jerusalem and of Samaria;

verses.rationale: Retain threatened analogy and two cities.
verses.before: will I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?
verses.after: As I did to Samaria and her idols, will I not do to Jerusalem and her images?’”
verses.tsw_comparator: will I not, as I have done to Samaria and her idols, so do to Jerusalem and her idols?

verses.rationale: Preserve third-to-first divine speech shift.
verses.before: So it will happen that, when the Lord has performed his whole work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the willful proud heart of the king of Assyria, and the insolence of his haughty looks.
verses.after: When the Lord has completed all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, “I will punish the fruit of Assyria’s king’s arrogant heart and his proudly lifted eyes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore it will happen that, when the Lord has performed his whole work on Mount Zion and on Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the willful proud heart of the king of Assyria, and the insolence of his haughty looks.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated self-credit, borders, and deposed rulers.
verses.before: For he has said, "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I have understanding: and I have removed the boundaries of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures. Like a valiant man I have brought down their rulers.
verses.after: For he says, “By my hand’s strength I did it, by my wisdom, for I am discerning. I removed peoples’ boundaries, plundered their treasures, and brought down those enthroned like a mighty one.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he has said, "By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; for I have understanding: and I have removed the boundaries of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures. Like a valiant man I have brought down their rulers.

verses.rationale: Retain nest simile and three resistance negatives.
verses.before: My hand has found the riches of the peoples like a nest, and like one gathers eggs that are abandoned, have I gathered all the earth. There was no one who moved their wing, or that opened their mouth, or chirped."
verses.after: My hand found the peoples’ wealth like a nest. As one gathers abandoned eggs, I gathered all the earth. No wing fluttered, no mouth opened, no chirp was heard.”
verses.tsw_comparator: My hand has found the riches of the peoples like a nest, and like one gathers eggs that are abandoned, have I gathered all the earth. There was no one who moved their wing, or that opened their mouth, or chirped."

verses.rationale: Keep four tool inversions and not-wood punchline.
verses.before: Should an axe brag against the one who chops with it? Should a saw exalt itself above the one who saws with it? As if a rod should lift people who lift it up, or as if a staff should lift up someone who is not wood.
verses.after: Does an ax boast over the one who chops with it? Does a saw exalt itself over the one who moves it? As if a rod could swing the one lifting it, or a staff lift someone who is not wood!
verses.tsw_comparator: Should an axe brag against the one who chops with it? Should a saw exalt itself above the one who saws with it? As if a rod should lift those who lift it up, or as if a staff should lift up someone who is not wood.

verses.rationale: Retain fat/thin reversal and burning glory.
verses.before: So the Lord GOD of Hosts, will send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory a burning will be kindled like the burning of fire.
verses.after: Therefore the Lord, the **LORD** of hosts, will send wasting sickness among his well-fed men; beneath his glory a blaze will burn like fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts, will send among his fat ones leanness; and under his glory a burning will be kindled like the burning of fire.

verses.rationale: Preserve two divine images and one-day destruction.
verses.before: The light of Israel will be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame; and it will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.
verses.after: Israel’s Light will become a fire, its Holy One a flame, burning and consuming his thorns and briers in a single day.
verses.tsw_comparator: The light of Israel will be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame; and it will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in one day.

verses.rationale: Retain forest/land, whole-being, and difficult wasting simile.
verses.before: He will consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body. It will be as when a standard bearer faints.
verses.after: The splendor of his forest and fruitful land he will consume, soul and body; it will be like a sick person wasting away.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will consume the glory of his forest, and of his fruitful field, both soul and body. It will be as when a standard bearer faints.

verses.rationale: Keep child-countable remnant.
verses.before: The remnant of the trees of his forest will be few, so that a child could write their number.
verses.after: So few trees will remain in his forest that a child could write down their number.
verses.tsw_comparator: The remnant of the trees of his forest will be few, so that a child could write their number.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated leaning and changed dependence.
verses.before: It will come to pass on that day that the remnant of Israel, and people who have escaped from the house of Jacob will no more again lean on the one who struck them, but will lean on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.
verses.after: On that day Israel’s remnant, the survivors of the house of Jacob, will no longer lean on the one who struck them. They will truly lean on the **LORD**, the Holy One of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will come to pass in that day that the remnant of Israel, and those who have escaped from the house of Jacob will no more again lean on the one who struck them, but will lean on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.

verses.rationale: Keep Shear-jashub echo and9:6 title.
verses.before: A remnant will return, even the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.
verses.after: A remnant will return, Jacob’s remnant, to the Mighty God.
verses.tsw_comparator: A remnant will return, even the remnant of Jacob, to the mighty God.

verses.rationale: Preserve multitude/remnant tension and flood image.
verses.before: For though your people, Israel, are like the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return. A destruction is determined, overflowing with righteousness.
verses.after: Though your people Israel are like the sand of the sea, only a remnant will return. Destruction is decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
verses.tsw_comparator: For though your people, Israel, are like the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return. A destruction is determined, overflowing with righteousness.

verses.rationale: Keep complete decree and divine title.
verses.before: For the Lord GOD of Hosts, will make a full end, and that determined, among all the earth.
