verses.after: The Lord **GOD** of hosts will carry out the decreed destruction throughout the whole land.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Lord GOD of Hosts, will make a full end, and that determined, in the midst of all the earth.

verses.rationale: Retain actual threat within reassurance.
verses.before: So the Lord GOD of Hosts, says "My people who dwell in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrian, though he strike you with the rod, and lift up his staff against you, as Egypt did.
verses.after: Therefore the Lord **GOD** of hosts says, “My people who live in Zion, do not fear Assyria when he strikes you with a rod and raises his staff against you as Egypt did.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the Lord GOD of Hosts, says "My people who dwell in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrian, though he strike you with the rod, and lift up his staff against you, as Egypt did.

verses.rationale: Keep short interval and redirected anger.
verses.before: For yet a very little while, and the indignation against you will be accomplished, and my anger will be directed to his destruction."
verses.after: In a very little while my indignation will end, and my anger will turn to their destruction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For yet a very little while, and the indignation against you will be accomplished, and my anger will be directed to his destruction."

verses.rationale: Retain two historical comparisons and Oreb.
verses.before: The LORD of Hosts will stir up a scourge against him, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb. His rod will be over the sea, and he will lift it up like he did against Egypt.
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts will raise a whip against him, as when he struck Midian at the rock of Oreb. His staff will be over the sea, raised as it was against Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD of Hosts will stir up a scourge against him, as in the slaughter of Midian at the rock of Oreb. His rod will be over the sea, and he will lift it up like he did against Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserve difficult fatness wording rather than import anointing.
verses.before: It will happen on that day, that his burden will depart from off your shoulder, and his yoke from off your neck, and the yoke will be destroyed because of the anointing oil.
verses.after: On that day his burden will leave your shoulder, his yoke your neck; the yoke will break because of fatness.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen in that day, that his burden will depart from off your shoulder, and his yoke from off your neck, and the yoke will be destroyed because of the anointing oil.

verses.rationale: Keep invasion itinerary and supply point.
verses.before: He has come to Aiath. He has passed through Migron. At Michmash he stores his baggage.
verses.after: He has reached Aiath, passed through Migron; at Michmash he stores his equipment.
verses.tsw_comparator: He has come to Aiath. He has passed through Migron. At Michmash he stores his baggage.

verses.rationale: Retain quoted army voice and towns’ reactions.
verses.before: They have gone over the pass. They have taken up their lodging at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul has fled.
verses.after: They cross the pass: “Geba will be our lodging.” Ramah trembles; Saul’s Gibeah flees.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have gone over the pass. They have taken up their lodging at Geba. Ramah trembles. Gibeah of Saul has fled.

verses.rationale: Keep three place names and exclamations.
verses.before: Cry aloud with your voice, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! You poor Anathoth!
verses.after: Cry out, daughter Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
verses.tsw_comparator: Cry aloud with your voice, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! You poor Anathoth!

verses.rationale: Preserve two evacuating communities.
verses.before: Madmenah is a fugitive. The inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety.
verses.after: Madmenah has fled; Gebim’s inhabitants seek safety.
verses.tsw_comparator: Madmenah is a fugitive. The inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety.

verses.rationale: Follow daughter read form and immediate menace.
verses.before: This very day he will halt at Nob. He shakes his hand at the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
verses.after: This very day he halts at Nob, shaking his hand at Daughter Zion’s mountain, at Jerusalem’s hill.
verses.tsw_comparator: This very day he will halt at Nob. He shakes his hand at the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keep height reversal and tree metaphor.
verses.before: Look, the Lord GOD of Hosts, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.
verses.after: Look! The Lord, the **LORD** of hosts, lops off the boughs with terrifying force. The tall trees are felled; the lofty are brought low.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the Lord GOD of Hosts, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.

verses.rationale: Retain iron and ambiguous mighty agent.
verses.before: He will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.
verses.after: He cuts down the forest thickets with iron; Lebanon falls by a mighty one.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will cut down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon will fall by the Mighty One.

verses.rationale: Keep stump-to-fruit movement and Jesse.
verses.before: A shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots will bear fruit.
verses.after: A shoot will grow from Jesse’s stump; a branch from his roots will bear fruit.
verses.tsw_comparator: A shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots will bear fruit.

verses.rationale: Preserve three pairs and repeated spirit.
verses.before: The Spirit of the LORD will rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
verses.after: The spirit of the **LORD** will rest upon him: a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and strength, a spirit of knowledge and fear of the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Spirit of the LORD will rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retain delight interpretation and sensory limits.
verses.before: His delight will be in the fear of the LORD. He will not judge by the sight of his eyes, neither decide by the hearing of his ears;
verses.after: His delight will be in the fear of the **LORD**. He will not judge by what his eyes see or decide by what his ears hear.
verses.tsw_comparator: His delight will be in the fear of the LORD. He will not judge by the sight of his eyes, neither decide by the hearing of his ears;

verses.rationale: Preserve justice, earth reading, and lethal speech.
verses.before: but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.
verses.after: He will judge the poor with righteousness and decide fairly for the earth’s afflicted. He will strike the earth with his mouth’s rod and kill the wicked with his lips’ breath.
verses.tsw_comparator: but with righteousness he will judge the poor, and decide with equity for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth; and with the breath of his lips he will kill the wicked.

verses.rationale: Keep two ethical belts.
verses.before: Righteousness will be the belt of his waist, and faithfulness the belt of his waist.
verses.after: Righteousness will be the belt at his waist, faithfulness the belt at his hips.
verses.tsw_comparator: Righteousness will be the belt of his waist, and faithfulness the belt of his waist.

verses.rationale: Retain all animals, including fattened animal.
verses.before: The wolf will dwell with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; the calf, the young lion, and the fattened animal together, and a little child will lead them.
verses.after: A wolf will live with a lamb; a leopard will lie down with a young goat. Calf, young lion, and fattened animal will be together, and a little child will lead them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wolf will dwell with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat; the calf, the young lion, and the fattened animal together, and a little child will lead them.

verses.rationale: Keep shared diet and offspring.
verses.before: The cow and the bear will graze. Their young ones will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.
verses.after: Cow and bear will graze; their young will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like cattle.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cow and the bear will graze. Their young ones will lie down together. The lion will eat straw like the ox.

verses.rationale: Retain two childhood stages and dangerous snakes.
verses.before: The nursing child will play near a cobra's hole, and the weaned child will put his hand on the viper's den.
verses.after: A nursing child will play by a cobra’s hole; a weaned child will reach into a viper’s den.
verses.tsw_comparator: The nursing child will play near a cobra's hole, and the weaned child will put his hand on the viper's den.

verses.rationale: Keep divine my and knowledge-filled world.
verses.before: They will not hurt or destroy on all my holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
verses.after: They will neither harm nor destroy on all my holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the **LORD**, as water covers the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will not hurt or destroy on all my holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.

verses.rationale: Retain root/person transition and national seeking.
verses.before: It will happen on that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.
verses.after: On that day Jesse’s root will stand as a signal for peoples. Nations will seek him, and his resting place will be glorious.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.

verses.rationale: Preserve second recovery and all eight locations.
verses.before: It will happen on that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.
verses.after: On that day the Lord will again extend his hand, a second time, to recover the remnant of his people left in Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the sea’s coastlands.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen in that day that the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.

verses.rationale: Keep two peoples and four corners.
verses.before: He will set up a banner for the nations, and will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
verses.after: He will raise a signal for the nations, gather Israel’s outcasts, and assemble Judah’s scattered people from the earth’s four corners.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will set up a banner for the nations, and will assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

verses.rationale: Retain reciprocal reconciled hostility.
verses.before: The envy also of Ephraim will depart, and people who persecute Judah will be cut off. Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not persecute Ephraim.
verses.after: Ephraim’s jealousy will depart, and Judah’s adversaries will be cut off. Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not harass Ephraim.
verses.tsw_comparator: The envy also of Ephraim will depart, and those who persecute Judah will be cut off. Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not persecute Ephraim.

verses.rationale: Preserve conquest alongside preceding peace imagery.
verses.before: They will fly down on the shoulders of the Philistines on the west. Together they will plunder the children of the east. They will extend their power over Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon will obey them.
verses.after: Together they will swoop on Philistia’s western slopes and plunder the people of the east. Edom and Moab will fall under their hand; the Ammonites will obey them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will fly down on the shoulders of the Philistines on the west. Together they will plunder the children of the east. They will extend their power over Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon will obey them.

verses.rationale: Keep sea tongue, wind, seven streams, sandals.
verses.before: The LORD will utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his scorching wind he will wave his hand over the River, and will split it into seven streams, and cause men to march over in sandals.
verses.after: The **LORD** will utterly destroy the tongue of Egypt’s sea. He will wave his hand over the River with his scorching wind, strike it into seven streams, and let people cross in sandals.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his scorching wind he will wave his hand over the River, and will split it into seven streams, and cause men to march over in sandals.

verses.rationale: Retain explicit exodus analogy.
verses.before: There will be a highway for the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, like there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.after: There will be a highway for the remnant of his people left in Assyria, as there was for Israel on the day it came up from Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: There will be a highway for the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, like there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Keep thanks after anger, comfort transition.
verses.before: On that day you will say, "I will give thanks to you, the LORD; for though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away and you comfort me.
verses.after: On that day you will say: “I thank you, **LORD**. Though you were angry with me, your anger turned away, and you comforted me.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day you will say, "I will give thanks to you, the LORD; for though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away and you comfort me.

verses.rationale: Retain both divine forms and exodus song echo.
verses.before: Look, God is my salvation; I will trust and will not be afraid, for the LORD, the LORD, is my strength and my song, and has become my salvation.
verses.after: Look, God is my salvation! I will trust and not be afraid. For **YAH**, the **LORD**, is my strength and song; he has become my salvation.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, God is my salvation; I will trust and will not be afraid, for the LORD, the LORD, is my strength and my song, and has become my salvation.

verses.rationale: Keep plural audience and water image.
verses.before: So with joy you will draw water out of the wells of salvation.
verses.after: With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore with joy you will draw water out of the wells of salvation.

verses.rationale: Preserve four communal imperatives.
verses.before: On that day you will say, "Give thanks to the LORD! Call on his name. Declare his doings among the peoples. Proclaim that his name is exalted!
verses.after: On that day you will say: “Thank the **LORD**; call on his name. Make his deeds known among the peoples; proclaim that his name is exalted.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day you will say, "Give thanks to the LORD! Call on his name. Declare his doings among the peoples. Proclaim that his name is exalted!

verses.rationale: Retain global announcement and read-form passive.
verses.before: Sing to the LORD, for he has done excellent things! Let this be known in all the earth!
verses.after: Sing to the **LORD**, for he has done glorious things. Let this be known throughout the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing to the LORD, for he has done excellent things! Let this be known in all the earth!

verses.rationale: Keep female city address and divine nearness.
verses.before: Cry aloud and shout, you inhabitant of Zion; for the Holy One of Israel is great among you!"
verses.after: Shout and sing for joy, you who dwell in Zion! Great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Cry aloud and shout, you inhabitant of Zion; for the Holy One of Israel is great in the midst of you!"

verses.rationale: Retain oracle and vision attribution.
verses.before: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw:
verses.after: An oracle concerning Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw:

verses.rationale: Keep three military signals and entrance.
verses.before: Set up a banner on the bare mountain! Lift up your voice to them! Wave your hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.
verses.after: Raise a signal on a bare hill! Shout to them; wave your hand, so they may enter the nobles’ gates.
verses.tsw_comparator: Set up a banner on the bare mountain! Lift up your voice to them! Wave your hand, that they may go into the gates of the nobles.

verses.rationale: Preserve consecrated warriors without moral sanitizing.
verses.before: I have commanded my consecrated ones; yes, I have called my mighty men for my anger, even my proudly exulting ones.
verses.after: I have commanded my consecrated ones; I have summoned my warriors to carry out my anger, those who exult in my majesty.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have commanded my consecrated ones; yes, I have called my mighty men for my anger, even my proudly exulting ones.

verses.rationale: Retain heard gathering and divine commander.
verses.before: The noise of a multitude is in the mountains, as of a great people; the noise of an uproar of the kingdoms of the nations gathered together! the LORD of Hosts is mustering the army for the battle.
verses.after: A roar on the mountains, like a vast people! The tumult of kingdoms, nations assembling! The **LORD** of hosts is mustering an army for war.
verses.tsw_comparator: The noise of a multitude is in the mountains, as of a great people; the noise of an uproar of the kingdoms of the nations gathered together! the LORD of Hosts is mustering the army for the battle.

verses.rationale: Keep distant origin and destructive purpose.
verses.before: They come from a far country, from the uttermost part of heaven, even the LORD, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.
verses.after: They come from a distant land, from the edge of the heavens— the **LORD** and the weapons of his fury— to ruin the whole land.
verses.tsw_comparator: They come from a far country, from the uttermost part of heaven, even the LORD, and the weapons of his indignation, to destroy the whole land.

verses.rationale: Retain Shaddai name and soundplay note.
verses.before: Wail; for the day of the LORD is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty.
verses.after: Wail, for the **LORD**’s day is near! It comes like devastation from Shaddai.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wail; for the day of the LORD is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty.

verses.rationale: Keep bodily fear metaphors.
verses.before: So all hands will be feeble, and everyone's heart will melt.
verses.after: Therefore every hand will go limp, every human heart will melt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore all hands will be feeble, and everyone's heart will melt.

verses.rationale: Preserve childbirth simile and flaming faces.
verses.before: They will be dismayed. Pangs and sorrows will seize them. They will be in pain like a woman in labor. They will look in amazement one at another. Their faces will be faces of flame.
verses.after: They will be terrified. Pangs and anguish will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor. They will stare at one another in horror, their faces aflame.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will be dismayed. Pangs and sorrows will seize them. They will be in pain like a woman in labor. They will look in amazement one at another. Their faces will be faces of flame.

verses.rationale: Retain cruelty and exterminating judgment.
verses.before: Look, the day of the LORD comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy its sinners out of it.
verses.after: Look, the **LORD**’s day is coming, cruel, with fury and burning anger, to make the land desolate and destroy its sinners from it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the day of the LORD comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy its sinners out of it.

verses.rationale: Keep three cosmic lights extinguished.
verses.before: For the stars of the sky and its constellations will not give their light. The sun will be darkened in its going forth, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.
verses.after: Heaven’s stars and constellations will not shine their light. The sun will be dark as it rises, and the moon will give no light.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the stars of the sky and its constellations will not give their light. The sun will be darkened in its going forth, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.

verses.rationale: Retain world scope and pride reversal.
verses.before: I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity. I will cause the arrogance of the proud to cease, and will humble the haughtiness of the terrible.
verses.after: “I will punish the world for its evil, the wicked for their guilt. I will end the arrogant’s pride and bring tyrants’ haughtiness low.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity. I will cause the arrogance of the proud to cease, and will humble the haughtiness of the terrible.

verses.rationale: Keep depopulation rather than increased value alone.
verses.before: I will make people more rare than fine gold, even a person than the pure gold of Ophir.
verses.after: I will make people scarcer than refined gold, human beings rarer than Ophir’s gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will make people more rare than fine gold, even a person than the pure gold of Ophir.

verses.rationale: Retain cosmic displacement and divine wrath.
verses.before: So I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will be shaken out of its place in the wrath of the LORD of Hosts, and in the day of his fierce anger.
verses.after: Therefore I will shake the heavens, and the earth will tremble out of place, at the **LORD** of hosts’ fury, on the day of his burning anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will be shaken out of its place in the wrath of the LORD of Hosts, and in the day of his fierce anger.

verses.rationale: Keep displaced multinationals and two similes.
verses.before: It will happen that like a a hunted gazelle, and like sheep that no one gathers, they will each turn to their own people, and will each flee to their own land.
verses.after: Like a hunted gazelle, like sheep with no one to gather them, each will turn to their own people, each flee to their own land.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen that like a a hunted gazelle, and like sheep that no one gathers, they will each turn to their own people, and will each flee to their own land.

verses.rationale: Retain comprehensive killing.
verses.before: Everyone who is found will be thrust through. Everyone who is captured will fall by the sword.
verses.after: Everyone found will be pierced through; everyone caught will fall by the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone who is found will be thrust through. Everyone who is captured will fall by the sword.

verses.rationale: Name all three harms explicitly, including sexual violence.
verses.before: Their infants also will be dashed in pieces before their eyes. Their houses will be ransacked, and their wives raped.
verses.after: Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses plundered, and their wives raped.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their infants also will be dashed in pieces before their eyes. Their houses will be ransacked, and their wives raped.

verses.rationale: Keep named attackers and unbribability.
verses.before: Look, I will stir up the Medes against them, who will not value silver, and as for gold, they will not delight in it.
verses.after: Look, I am stirring up the Medes against them, who care nothing for silver and take no pleasure in gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I will stir up the Medes against them, who will not value silver, and as for gold, they will not delight in it.

verses.rationale: Preserve violence against young and unborn/offspring ambiguity.
verses.before: Their bows will dash the young men in pieces; and they will have no pity on the fruit of the womb. Their eyes will not spare children.
verses.after: Their bows will shatter young men. They will have no mercy on the fruit of the womb; their eyes will not spare children.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their bows will dash the young men in pieces; and they will have no pity on the fruit of the womb. Their eyes will not spare children.

verses.rationale: Keep Chaldeans and overthrow analogy.
verses.before: Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldeans' pride, will be like when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
verses.after: Babylon, beauty among kingdoms, the Chaldeans’ proud splendor, will be like Sodom and Gomorrah when God overthrew them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldeans' pride, will be like when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

verses.rationale: Preserve absolute desolation and named nomadic inhabitant.
verses.before: It will never be inhabited, neither will it be lived in from generation to generation. The Arabian will not pitch a tent there, neither will shepherds make their flocks lie down there.
verses.after: It will never again be inhabited or settled through the generations. No Arab will pitch a tent there; no shepherd will rest a flock there.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will never be inhabited, neither will it be lived in from generation to generation. The Arabian will not pitch a tent there, neither will shepherds make their flocks lie down there.

verses.rationale: Keep eerie fauna with uncertain identifications noted.
verses.before: But wild animals of the desert will lie there, and their houses will be full of jackals. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will frolic there.
verses.after: Desert creatures will lie there; its houses will fill with howling animals. Ostriches will live there, and goat-demons will dance there.
verses.tsw_comparator: But wild animals of the desert will lie there, and their houses will be full of jackals. Ostriches will dwell there, and wild goats will frolic there.

verses.rationale: Retain answering animals and imminent end.
verses.before: Wolves will cry in their castles, and jackals in the pleasant palaces. Her time is near to come, and her days will not be prolonged.
verses.after: Hyenas will answer one another in its fortresses, jackals in its luxurious palaces. Its time is near; its days will not be prolonged.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Wolves will cry in their castles, and jackals in the pleasant palaces. Her time is near to come, and her days will not be prolonged.

verses.rationale: Keep renewed election and attached foreigners.
verses.before: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land. The foreigner will join himself with them, and they will unite with the house of Jacob.
verses.after: The **LORD** will have compassion on Jacob and again choose Israel. He will settle them on their own land. Resident foreigners will join them and attach themselves to the house of Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land. The foreigner will join himself with them, and they will unite with the house of Jacob.

verses.rationale: Preserve slavery reversal without euphemism.
verses.before: The peoples will take them, and bring them to their place. The house of Israel will possess them in the LORD's land for servants and for handmaids. They will take as captives those whose captives they were; and they will rule over their oppressors.
verses.after: Peoples will bring them to their own place, and the house of Israel will possess those peoples as male and female slaves in the **LORD**’s land. They will capture their captors and rule over their oppressors.
verses.tsw_comparator: The peoples will take them, and bring them to their place. The house of Israel will possess them in the LORD's land for servants and for handmaids. They will take as captives those whose captives they were; and they will rule over their oppressors.

verses.rationale: Keep three burdens and forced labor.
verses.before: It will happen in the day that the LORD will give you rest from your sorrow, from your trouble, and from the hard service in which you were made to serve,
verses.after: When the **LORD** gives you rest from pain, turmoil, and the harsh labor forced upon you,
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen in the day that the LORD will give you rest from your sorrow, from your trouble, and from the hard service in which you were made to serve,

verses.rationale: Retain the human royal target and a gold-exaction sense for rare madhebah; distinguish the emended fury reading in a note.
verses.before: that you will take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and say, "How the oppressor has ceased! The golden city has ceased!"
verses.after: you will take up this taunt against Babylon’s king: “How the oppressor has stopped! How his extortion has ended!
verses.tsw_comparator: that you will take up this parable against the king of Babylon, and say, "How the oppressor has ceased! The golden city has ceased!"

verses.rationale: Keep broken instruments of power.
verses.before: The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers,
verses.after: The **LORD** has broken the wicked’s staff, the rulers’ rod,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers,

verses.rationale: Retain relentless violence and parallel ruling.
verses.before: who struck the peoples in wrath with a continual stroke, who ruled the nations in anger, with a persecution that none restrained.
verses.after: which struck peoples in fury with blows that never stopped, which ruled nations in anger with unrelenting pursuit.
verses.tsw_comparator: who struck the peoples in wrath with a continual stroke, who ruled the nations in anger, with a persecution that none restrained.

verses.rationale: Keep earth’s audible relief.
verses.before: The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet. They break out song.
verses.after: All the earth rests, quiet at last; it breaks into joyful song.
verses.tsw_comparator: The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet. They break out song.

verses.rationale: Preserve trees’ quoted relief from extraction.
verses.before: Yes, the fir trees rejoice with you, with the cedars of Lebanon, saying, "Since you are humbled, no lumberjack has come up against us."
verses.after: Even the cypresses rejoice over you, and Lebanon’s cedars: ‘Since you were laid low, no woodcutter comes against us.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Yes, the fir trees rejoice with you, with the cedars of Lebanon, saying, "Since you are humbled, no lumberjack has come up against us."

verses.rationale: Keep personified underworld and dead rulers.
verses.before: Sheol from beneath has moved for you to meet you at your coming. It stirs up the dead for you, even all the rulers of the earth. It has raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
verses.after: Sheol below stirs to meet you when you come. It rouses the shades for you, all the earth’s leaders; it lifts from their thrones all the kings of nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sheol from beneath has moved for you to meet you at your coming. It stirs up the dead for you, even all the rulers of the earth. It has raised up from their thrones all the kings of the nations.

verses.rationale: Retain mocking equalization.
verses.before: They all will answer and ask you, "Have you also become as weak as we are? Have you become like us?"
verses.after: They all answer you: ‘You too have become weak like us! You have become one of us!’
verses.tsw_comparator: They all will answer and ask you, "Have you also become as weak as we are? Have you become like us?"

verses.rationale: Preserve decaying royal bed image.
verses.before: Your pomp is brought down to Sheol, with the sound of your stringed instruments. Maggots are spread out under you, and worms cover you.
verses.after: Your pomp has been brought down to Sheol, with the sound of your harps. Maggots are spread beneath you; worms are your covering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your pomp is brought down to Sheol, with the sound of your stringed instruments. Maggots are spread out under you, and worms cover you.

verses.rationale: Retain celestial title within king’s taunt, no inserted Satan.
verses.before: How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of dawn! You have been cut down to the ground, you who laid nations low.
verses.after: How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of Dawn! You are cut down to the earth, you who laid nations low.
verses.tsw_comparator: How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of dawn! You have been cut down to the ground, you who laid nations low.

verses.rationale: Keep royal ascent and mythic place term.
verses.before: You said in your heart, "I will ascend into heaven! I will exalt my throne above the stars of God! I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far north!
verses.after: You said in your heart, ‘I will ascend to heaven; above God’s stars I will raise my throne. I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far reaches of Zaphon.
verses.tsw_comparator: You said in your heart, "I will ascend into heaven! I will exalt my throne above the stars of God! I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far north!

verses.rationale: Preserve two self-exalting claims.
verses.before: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most High!"
verses.after: I will ascend above the cloud heights; I will make myself like the Most High.’
verses.tsw_comparator: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most High!"

verses.rationale: Keep ascent/descent reversal.
verses.before: Yet you will be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.
verses.after: But down to Sheol you are brought, to the deepest reaches of the Pit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet you will be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.

verses.rationale: Retain explicit man and astonishment.
verses.before: People who see you will stare at you. They will ponder you, saying, "Is this the man who made the earth to tremble, who shook kingdoms;
verses.after: Those who see you will stare and ponder: ‘Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms,
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who see you will stare at you. They will ponder you, saying, "Is this the man who made the earth to tremble, who shook kingdoms;

verses.rationale: Keep three destructive royal acts.
verses.before: who made the world like a wilderness, and overthrew its cities; who did not release his prisoners to their home?"
verses.after: who made the world a wilderness and demolished its cities, who would not release his prisoners to go home?’
verses.tsw_comparator: who made the world like a wilderness, and overthrew its cities; who did not release his prisoners to their home?"

verses.rationale: Retain universal royal burial contrast.
verses.before: All the kings of the nations, sleep in glory, everyone in his own house.
verses.after: All the kings of nations lie in honor, each in his own tomb.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the kings of the nations, sleep in glory, everyone in his own house.

verses.rationale: Keep unburied body and difficult layered images.
verses.before: But you are cast away from your tomb like an abominable branch, clothed with the slain, who are thrust through with the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit; like a dead body trodden under foot.
verses.after: But you are thrown away from your grave like a despised branch, clothed with the slain, pierced by swords, who go down to the stones of the Pit— like a corpse trampled underfoot.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you are cast away from your tomb like an abominable branch, clothed with the slain, who are thrust through with the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit; like a dead body trodden under foot.

verses.rationale: Preserve explanation and curse on descendants.
verses.before: You will not join them in burial, because you have destroyed your land. You have killed your people. The seed of evil-doers will not be named forever.
verses.after: You will not join them in burial, for you ruined your land and killed your people. May evildoers’ offspring never be named again!
verses.tsw_comparator: You will not join them in burial, because you have destroyed your land. You have killed your people. The seed of evil-doers will not be named forever.

verses.rationale: Retain intergenerational violence and cities text.
verses.before: Prepare for slaughter of his children because of the iniquity of their fathers, that they not rise up and possess the earth, and fill the surface of the world with cities.
verses.after: Prepare a slaughtering place for his sons because of their fathers’ guilt, so they cannot rise and possess the land and fill the world’s surface with cities.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Prepare for slaughter of his children because of the iniquity of their fathers, that they not rise up and possess the earth, and fill the surface of the world with cities.

verses.rationale: Keep doubled declaration and four removals.
verses.before: "I will rise up against them," says the LORD of Hosts, "and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, and son and son's son," says the LORD.
verses.after: “I will rise against them,” declares the **LORD** of hosts. “I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and descendants,” declares the **LORD**.
verses.tsw_comparator: "I will rise up against them," says the LORD of Hosts, "and cut off from Babylon name and remnant, and son and son's son," says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve animal uncertainty in note and broom image.
verses.before: "I will also make it a possession for the porcupine, and pools of water. I will sweep it with the broom of destruction," says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: “I will make it a possession for hedgehogs and pools of water. I will sweep it with the broom of destruction,” declares the **LORD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: "I will also make it a possession for the porcupine, and pools of water. I will sweep it with the broom of destruction," says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retain oath and parallel resolve.
verses.before: The LORD of Hosts has sworn, saying, "Surely, as I have thought, so will it happen; and as I have purposed, so will it stand:
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts has sworn: “As I have intended, so it will happen; as I have planned, so it will stand:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD of Hosts has sworn, saying, "Surely, as I have thought, so will it happen; and as I have purposed, so will it stand:

verses.rationale: Keep land claim and freed burden.
verses.before: that I will break the Assyrian in my land, and tread him under foot on my mountains. Then his yoke will leave them, and his burden leave their shoulders.
verses.after: I will break Assyria in my land, trample him on my mountains. His yoke will leave them; his burden will leave their shoulders.”
verses.tsw_comparator: that I will break the Assyrian in my land, and tread him under foot on my mountains. Then his yoke will leave them, and his burden leave their shoulders.

verses.rationale: Retain global reach and stretched hand.
verses.before: This is the plan that is determined for the entire earth. This is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.
verses.after: This is the plan made for all the earth; this is the hand stretched over all the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the plan that is determined for the whole earth. This is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.

verses.rationale: Keep two rhetorical challenges.
verses.before: For the LORD of Hosts has planned, and who can stop it? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?"
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts has planned it—who can thwart it? His hand is stretched out—who can turn it back?
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD of Hosts has planned, and who can stop it? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?"

verses.rationale: Preserve chronological heading.
verses.before: This burden was in the year that king Ahaz died.
verses.after: This oracle came in the year King Ahaz died:
verses.tsw_comparator: This burden was in the year that king Ahaz died.

verses.rationale: Keep succession of snake images without historical identification.
verses.before: Don't rejoice, O Philistia, all of you, because the rod that struck you is broken; for out of the serpent's root an adder will emerge, and his fruit will be a fiery flying serpent.
verses.after: Do not rejoice, all Philistia, that the rod striking you is broken. From the snake’s root a viper will come, and its fruit will be a flying fiery serpent.
verses.tsw_comparator: Don't rejoice, O Philistia, all of you, because the rod that struck you is broken; for out of the serpent's root an adder will emerge, and his fruit will be a fiery flying serpent.

verses.rationale: Retain poor’s safety versus Philistia’s famine.
verses.before: The firstborn of the poor will eat, and the needy will lie down in safety; and I will kill your root with famine, and your remnant will be killed.
verses.after: The poorest of the poor will graze, and the needy lie down safely. But I will kill your root with famine; it will slay your remnant.
verses.tsw_comparator: The firstborn of the poor will eat, and the needy will lie down in safety; and I will kill your root with famine, and your remnant will be killed.

verses.rationale: Keep city personification and organized army.
verses.before: Howl, gate! Cry, city! You are melted away, Philistia, all of you; for smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks.
verses.after: Wail, gate! Cry out, city! Melt away, all Philistia! Smoke comes from the north, and none strays from its ranks.
verses.tsw_comparator: Howl, gate! Cry, city! You are melted away, Philistia, all of you; for smoke comes out of the north, and there is no straggler in his ranks.

verses.rationale: Retain diplomatic question and refuge answer.
verses.before: What will they answer the messengers of the nation? That the LORD has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people will take refuge.
verses.after: What answer should be given to a nation’s messengers? “The **LORD** founded Zion, and his people’s afflicted find refuge there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: What will they answer the messengers of the nation? That the LORD has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people will take refuge.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated night and two cities.
verses.before: The burden of Moab: for in a night, Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing; for in a night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing.
verses.after: An oracle concerning Moab: In a night Ar of Moab is devastated, silenced; in a night Kir of Moab is devastated, silenced.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burden of Moab: for in a night, Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing; for in a night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing.

verses.rationale: Retain local mourning rites and names.
verses.before: They have gone up to Bayith, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba. Baldness is on all of their heads. Every beard is cut off.
verses.after: Moab has gone up to the temple, to Dibon’s high places, to weep. Over Nebo and Medeba it wails. Every head is shaved; every beard is cut off.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have gone up to Bayith, and to Dibon, to the high places, to weep. Moab wails over Nebo and over Medeba. Baldness is on all of their heads. Every beard is cut off.

verses.rationale: Keep public spaces and bodily grief.
verses.before: In their streets, they dress themselves in sackcloth. In their streets and on their housetops, everyone wails, weeping abundantly.
verses.after: In its streets they wear sackcloth; on rooftops and in squares everyone wails, melting into tears.
verses.tsw_comparator: In their streets, they dress themselves in sackcloth. In their streets and on their housetops, everyone wails, weeping abundantly.

verses.rationale: Retain soldiers’ grief and three towns.
verses.before: Heshbon cries out with Elealeh. Their voice is heard even to Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud. Their souls tremble within them.
verses.after: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. So Moab’s armed men cry aloud; its very life trembles.
verses.tsw_comparator: Heshbon cries out with Elealeh. Their voice is heard even to Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud. Their souls tremble within them.

verses.rationale: Keep first-person compassion and flight route.
verses.before: My heart cries out for Moab! Her nobles flee to Zoar, to Eglath Shelishiyah; for they go up by the ascent of Luhith with weeping; for in the way of Horonaim, they raise up a cry of destruction.
verses.after: My heart cries out for Moab. Its fugitives reach Zoar, Eglath-shelishiyah. They climb Luhith’s ascent weeping; on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: My heart cries out for Moab! Her nobles flee to Zoar, to Eglath Shelishiyah; for they go up by the ascent of Luhith with weeping; for in the way of Horonaim, they raise up a cry of destruction.

verses.rationale: Retain water loss and three vegetation failures.
verses.before: For the waters of Nimrim will be desolate; for the grass has withered away, the tender grass fails, there is no green thing.
verses.after: Nimrim’s waters are desolate; the grass has dried, new growth has ended, and nothing green remains.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the waters of Nimrim will be desolate; for the grass has withered away, the tender grass fails, there is no green thing.

verses.rationale: Keep refugees’ possessions and named crossing.
verses.before: So they will carry away the abundance they have gotten, and what they have stored up, over the brook of the willows.
verses.after: So the wealth they have gained, all they have stored, they carry across the Wadi of the Willows.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore they will carry away the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have stored up, over the brook of the willows.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated wailing and geographical extent.
verses.before: For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab; its wailing to Eglaim, and its wailing to Beer Elim.
verses.after: The cry circles Moab’s borders; its wailing reaches Eglaim, its wailing reaches Beer-elim.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab; its wailing to Eglaim, and its wailing to Beer Elim.

verses.rationale: Keep blood, added judgment, and surviving targets.
verses.before: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring yet more on Dimon, a lion on those of Moab who escape, and on the remnant of the land.
verses.after: Dimon’s waters are full of blood, yet I will bring more upon Dimon: a lion against Moab’s fugitives and those left in the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring yet more on Dimon, a lion on those of Moab who escape, and on the remnant of the land.

verses.rationale: Preserve tribute and route; singular lamb retained.
verses.before: Send the lambs for the ruler of the land from Selah to the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
verses.after: Send a lamb to the ruler of the land, from Sela through the wilderness to Daughter Zion’s mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Send the lambs for the ruler of the land from Selah to the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.

verses.rationale: Retain female fugitives and nest image.
verses.before: For it will be that as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.
verses.after: Like wandering birds, like a scattered nest, Moab’s daughters will be at the Arnon crossings.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it will be that as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.

verses.rationale: Keep protection petition and noon/night contrast.
verses.before: Give counsel! Execute justice! Make your shade like the night among the noonday! Hide the outcasts! Don't betray the fugitive!
verses.after: “Give counsel; render judgment. At noon make your shade like night. Hide the outcasts; do not betray the fugitive.
verses.tsw_comparator: Give counsel! Execute justice! Make your shade like the night in the midst of the noonday! Hide the outcasts! Don't betray the fugitive!

verses.rationale: Follow my-outcasts vocalization; alternative Moab’s outcasts noted.
verses.before: Let my outcasts dwell with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortioner is brought to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.
verses.after: Let my outcasts live with you, Moab; be a hiding place for them from the destroyer. For the extortioner is gone, destruction has ended, the trampler has vanished from the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let my outcasts dwell with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortioner is brought to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.

verses.rationale: Preserve Davidic tent and three judicial actions.
verses.before: A throne will be established in steadfast love. One will sit on it in truth, in the tent of David, judging, seeking justice, and swift to do righteousness.
verses.after: A throne will be established in steadfast love, and on it, in David’s tent, one will sit faithfully, judging, seeking justice, and swift to do right.”
verses.tsw_comparator: A throne will be established in steadfast love. One will sit on it in truth, in the tent of David, judging, seeking justice, and swift to do righteousness.

verses.rationale: Retain piled pride terms.
verses.before: We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud; even of his arrogance, his pride, and his wrath. His boastings are nothing.
verses.after: We have heard of Moab’s pride—so very proud— its arrogance, pride, and fury. Its boasts are empty.
verses.tsw_comparator: We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud; even of his arrogance, his pride, and his wrath. His boastings are nothing.

verses.rationale: Keep repeated Moab and specific lost produce.
verses.before: So Moab will wail for Moab. Everyone will wail. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, utterly stricken.
verses.after: So Moab will wail for Moab; everyone will wail. For Kir-hareseth’s raisin cakes you will moan, utterly stricken.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore Moab will wail for Moab. Everyone will wail. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, utterly stricken.

verses.rationale: Preserve vine expansion and devastation.
verses.before: For the fields of Heshbon languish with the vine of Sibmah. The lords of the nations have broken down its choice branches, which reached even to Jazer, which wandered into the wilderness. Its shoots were spread abroad. They passed over the sea.
verses.after: Heshbon’s fields have withered, and Sibmah’s vine. Rulers of nations have struck down its choice branches, which reached Jazer and wandered into the wilderness; its shoots spread out and crossed the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the fields of Heshbon languish with the vine of Sibmah. The lords of the nations have broken down its choice branches, which reached even to Jazer, which wandered into the wilderness. Its shoots were spread abroad. They passed over the sea.

verses.rationale: Keep first-person lament and ambiguous shout.
verses.before: So I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah. I will water you with my tears, Heshbon, and Elealeh: for on your summer fruits and on your harvest the battle shout has fallen.
verses.after: So I weep with Jazer over Sibmah’s vine. I drench you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, for a shout has fallen on your summer fruit and harvest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah. I will water you with my tears, Heshbon, and Elealeh: for on your summer fruits and on your harvest the battle shout has fallen.

verses.rationale: Preserve divine/prophetic voice ambiguity and ended celebration.
verses.before: Gladness is taken away, and joy out of the fruitful field; and in the vineyards there will be no singing, neither joyful noise. Nobody will tread out wine in the presses. I have made the shouting stop.
verses.after: Joy and gladness are taken from fruitful fields; no singing, no shouting rings through the vineyards. No one treads wine in the presses. I have ended the harvest shout.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gladness is taken away, and joy out of the fruitful field; and in the vineyards there will be no singing, neither joyful noise. Nobody will tread out wine in the presses. I have made the shouting stop.

verses.rationale: Keep visceral musical lament.
verses.before: So my heart sounds like a harp for Moab, and my inward parts for Kir Heres.
verses.after: So my inward parts sound like a lyre for Moab, my very heart for Kir-heres.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore my heart sounds like a harp for Moab, and my inward parts for Kir Heres.

verses.rationale: Retain futile worship without additional polemic.
verses.before: It will happen that when Moab presents himself, when he wearies himself on the high place, and comes to his sanctuary to pray, that he will not prevail.
verses.after: When Moab appears at the high place and wears itself out, when it enters its sanctuary to pray, it will achieve nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen that when Moab presents himself, when he wearies himself on the high place, and comes to his sanctuary to pray, that he will not prevail.

verses.rationale: Keep earlier oracle distinction.
verses.before: This is the word that the LORD spoke concerning Moab in time past.
verses.after: This is the word the **LORD** spoke concerning Moab formerly.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the word that the LORD spoke concerning Moab in time past.

verses.rationale: Preserve exact contracted interval and reduced remnant.
verses.before: But now the LORD has spoken, saying, "Within three years, as a worker bound by contract would count them, the glory of Moab will be brought into contempt, with all his great multitude; and the remnant will be very small and feeble."
verses.after: Now the **LORD** says, “Within three years, counted like a hired worker’s years, Moab’s glory and all its great multitude will be brought low. The remnant will be very small and powerless.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But now the LORD has spoken, saying, "Within three years, as a worker bound by contract would count them, the glory of Moab will be brought into contempt, with all his great multitude; and the remnant will be very small and feeble."

verses.rationale: Retain named city’s erasure.
verses.before: The burden of Damascus: "Look, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it will be a ruinous heap.
verses.after: An oracle concerning Damascus: Look, Damascus will cease to be a city; it will become a heap of ruins.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burden of Damascus: "Look, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it will be a ruinous heap.

verses.rationale: Preserve Aroer and undisturbed flocks.
verses.before: The cities of Aroer are forsaken. They will be for flocks, which will lie down, and none will make them afraid.
verses.after: Aroer’s towns will be abandoned, left for flocks to lie down in, with no one to frighten them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cities of Aroer are forsaken. They will be for flocks, which will lie down, and none will make them afraid.

verses.rationale: Keep linked losses and ironic glory comparison.
verses.before: The fortress will cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria. They will be as the glory of the children of Israel," says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: Fortresses will disappear from Ephraim, royal power from Damascus. Aram’s remnant will be like Israel’s glory, declares the **LORD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fortress will cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria. They will be as the glory of the children of Israel," says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Preserve emaciation metaphor.
verses.before: "It will happen on that day that the glory of Jacob will be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh will become lean.
verses.after: On that day Jacob’s glory will grow thin, and his well-fed body waste away.
verses.tsw_comparator: "It will happen in that day that the glory of Jacob will be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh will become lean.

verses.rationale: Retain harvest/gleaning and named valley.
verses.before: It will be like when the harvester gathers the wheat, and his arm reaps the grain. Yes, it will be like when one gleans grain in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.after: It will be like a reaper gathering standing grain, his arm cutting the ears, like someone gleaning ears of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will be like when the harvester gathers the wheat, and his arm reaps the grain. Yes, it will be like when one gleans grain in the valley of Rephaim.

verses.rationale: Keep exact remnant numbers and olive image.
verses.before: Yet gleanings will be left there, like the shaking of an olive tree, two or three olives in the top of the uppermost bough, four or five in the outermost branches of a fruitful tree," says the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.after: Only gleanings will remain, as when an olive tree is beaten: two or three olives at the topmost branch, four or five on its fruitful boughs, declares the **LORD**, Israel’s God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet gleanings will be left there, like the shaking of an olive tree, two or three olives in the top of the uppermost bough, four or five in the outermost branches of a fruitful tree," says the LORD, the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retain maker/title and directed eyes.
verses.before: On that day, people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will have respect for the Holy One of Israel.
verses.after: On that day people will look to their Maker; their eyes will turn to the Holy One of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day, people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will have respect for the Holy One of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep human manufacture and named cultic objects.
verses.before: They will not look to the altars, the work of their hands; neither will they respect what their fingers have made, either the Asherim, or the incense altars.
verses.after: They will not look to the altars their hands made or regard what their fingers fashioned— the Asherah poles and incense stands.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will not look to the altars, the work of their hands; neither will they respect that which their fingers have made, either the Asherim, or the incense altars.

verses.rationale: Follow pinned woodland/hilltop wording, alternative noted.
verses.before: On that day, their strong cities will be like the forsaken places in the woods and on the mountain top, which were forsaken from before the children of Israel; and it will be a desolation.
verses.after: On that day their strong cities will be like abandoned woodland and hilltops, deserted before the Israelites. There will be desolation.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day, their strong cities will be like the forsaken places in the woods and on the mountain top, which were forsaken from before the children of Israel; and it will be a desolation.

verses.rationale: Preserve forget/remember and horticultural response.
verses.before: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation, and have not remembered the rock of your strength. Therefore you plant pleasant plants, and set out foreign seedlings.
verses.after: You have forgotten the God of your salvation and failed to remember the Rock of your refuge. So you plant delightful gardens and set them with foreign vine shoots.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you have forgotten the God of your salvation, and have not remembered the rock of your strength. Therefore you plant pleasant plants, and set out foreign seedlings.

verses.rationale: Keep accelerated growth and difficult vanishing harvest reading.
verses.before: In the day of your planting, you hedge it in. In the morning, you make your seed blossom, but the harvest flees away in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.
verses.after: You make them flourish the day you plant, and bloom the morning you sow. But the harvest flees on a day of sickness and incurable pain.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the day of your planting, you hedge it in. In the morning, you make your seed blossom, but the harvest flees away in the day of grief and of desperate sorrow.

verses.rationale: Retain repeated aquatic sound pattern.
verses.before: Ah, the uproar of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the seas; and the rushing of nations, that rush like the rushing of mighty waters!
verses.after: Ah, the uproar of many peoples, roaring like the seas! The crash of nations, crashing like mighty waters!
verses.tsw_comparator: Ah, the uproar of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the seas; and the rushing of nations, that rush like the rushing of mighty waters!

verses.rationale: Keep unexpressed divine subject and two dispersal images.
verses.before: The nations will rush like the rushing of many waters: but he will rebuke them, and they will flee far off, and will be chased like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like the whirling dust before the storm.
verses.after: Nations crash like surging waters, but he rebukes them and they flee far away, driven like mountain chaff before the wind, like tumbleweed before a storm.
verses.tsw_comparator: The nations will rush like the rushing of many waters: but he will rebuke them, and they will flee far off, and will be chased like the chaff of the mountains before the wind, and like the whirling dust before the storm.

verses.rationale: Retain overnight reversal and communal us.
verses.before: At evening, look, terror! Before the morning, they are no more. This is the portion of people who plunder us, and the lot of people who rob us.
verses.after: At evening—terror! Before morning—they are gone. This is the portion of those who plunder us, the lot of those who rob us.
verses.tsw_comparator: At evening, look, terror! Before the morning, they are no more. This is the portion of those who plunder us, and the lot of those who rob us.

verses.rationale: Keep uncertain wing image and Cush geography.
verses.before: Ah, the land of the rustling of wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia;
verses.after: Ah, land of whirring wings, beyond the rivers of Cush,
verses.tsw_comparator: Ah, the land of the rustling of wings, which is beyond the rivers of Ethiopia;

verses.rationale: Retain boats and difficult ethnographic descriptors without racial inference.
verses.before: that sends ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of papyrus on the waters, saying, "Go, you swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people awesome from their beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide!"
verses.after: sending envoys by water, in papyrus boats over the waters! Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth-skinned, to a people feared near and far, a powerful, trampling nation whose land the rivers divide.
verses.tsw_comparator: that sends ambassadors by the sea, even in vessels of papyrus on the waters, saying, "Go, you swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people awesome from their beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide!"

verses.rationale: Keep universal summons and sight/hearing commands.
verses.before: All you inhabitants of the world, and you dwellers on the earth, when a banner is lifted up on the mountains, look! When the trumpet is blown, listen!
verses.after: All who inhabit the world, all who dwell on earth: when a signal is raised on the mountains, look! When a horn is sounded, listen!
verses.tsw_comparator: All you inhabitants of the world, and you dwellers on the earth, when a banner is lifted up on the mountains, look! When the trumpet is blown, listen!

verses.rationale: Preserve divine waiting and two weather similes.
verses.before: For the LORD said to me, "I will be still, and I will see in my dwelling place, like clear heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."
verses.after: For the **LORD** told me: “I will remain still and watch from my dwelling, like clear heat in sunlight, like a cloud of dew in harvest heat.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD said to me, "I will be still, and I will see in my dwelling place, like clear heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."

verses.rationale: Keep preharvest timing and violent pruning.
verses.before: For before the harvest, when the blossom is over, and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and he will cut down and take away the spreading branches.
verses.after: Before harvest, when flowering ends and blossoms become ripening grapes, he will cut off the shoots with pruning hooks, remove and slash the spreading branches.
verses.tsw_comparator: For before the harvest, when the blossom is over, and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and he will cut down and take away the spreading branches.

verses.rationale: Preserve carcass implication and seasonal pair.
verses.before: They will be left together for the ravenous birds of the mountains, and for the animals of the earth. The ravenous birds will summer on them, and all the animals of the earth will winter on them.
verses.after: They will all be left for mountain birds of prey and wild animals. The birds will summer on them; the wild animals will winter on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will be left together for the ravenous birds of the mountains, and for the animals of the earth. The ravenous birds will summer on them, and all the animals of the earth will winter on them.

verses.rationale: Repeat national description and two divine names.
verses.before: In that time, a present will be brought to the LORD of Hosts from a people tall and smooth, even from a people awesome from their beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of the LORD of Hosts, Mount Zion.
verses.after: At that time tribute will be brought to the **LORD** of hosts from a people tall and smooth-skinned, a people feared near and far, a powerful, trampling nation whose land the rivers divide—to Mount Zion, the place of the name of the **LORD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that time, a present will be brought to the LORD of Hosts from a people tall and smooth, even from a people awesome from their beginning onward, a nation that measures out and treads down, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of the LORD of Hosts, Mount Zion.

verses.rationale: Retain cloud rider and idol/heart fear.
verses.before: The burden of Egypt: "Look, the LORD rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble at his presence; and the heart of Egypt will melt in its midst.
verses.after: An oracle concerning Egypt: Look, the **LORD** rides a swift cloud and comes to Egypt. Egypt’s idols tremble before him; Egypt’s heart melts within it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burden of Egypt: "Look, the LORD rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt. The idols of Egypt will tremble at his presence; and the heart of Egypt will melt in its midst.

verses.rationale: Preserve four escalating internal conflicts.
verses.before: I will stir up the Egyptians against the Egyptians, and they will fight everyone against his brother, and everyone against his neighbor; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
verses.after: “I will stir Egyptian against Egyptian. They will fight, brother against brother, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will stir up the Egyptians against the Egyptians, and they will fight everyone against his brother, and everyone against his neighbor; city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.

verses.rationale: Keep failed counsel and four recourses.
verses.before: The spirit of Egypt will fail in its midst. I will destroy its counsel. They will seek the idols, the charmers, people who have familiar spirits, and the wizards.
verses.after: Egypt’s spirit will drain away within it, and I will swallow up its plans. They will consult idols and ghosts, mediums and spiritists.
verses.tsw_comparator: The spirit of Egypt will fail in its midst. I will destroy its counsel. They will seek the idols, the charmers, those who have familiar spirits, and the wizards.

verses.rationale: Retain surrender and tyrannical king.
verses.before: I will give over the Egyptians into the hand of a cruel lord. A fierce king will rule over them," says the Lord GOD of Hosts.
verses.after: I will hand Egypt over to a harsh master; a fierce king will rule them,” declares the Lord, the **LORD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give over the Egyptians into the hand of a cruel lord. A fierce king will rule over them," says the Lord GOD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keep sea/river language in Egyptian setting.
verses.before: The waters will fail from the sea, and the river will be wasted and become dry.
verses.after: The sea’s waters will dry up; the River will be parched and dry.
verses.tsw_comparator: The waters will fail from the sea, and the river will be wasted and become dry.

verses.rationale: Retain stench, water loss, vegetation.
verses.before: The rivers will become foul. The streams of Egypt will be diminished and dried up. The reeds and flags will wither away.
verses.after: The channels will stink; Egypt’s streams will dwindle and dry. Reeds and rushes will wither.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rivers will become foul. The streams of Egypt will be diminished and dried up. The reeds and flags will wither away.

verses.rationale: Keep three-step crop disappearance.
verses.before: The meadows by the Nile, by the brink of the Nile, and all the sown fields of the Nile, will become dry, be driven away, and be no more.
verses.after: The riverbank growth, at the River’s edge, and every field sown beside it will dry up, blow away, and be gone.
verses.tsw_comparator: The meadows by the Nile, by the brink of the Nile, and all the sown fields of the Nile, will become dry, be driven away, and be no more.

verses.rationale: Preserve two fishing methods and livelihoods.
verses.before: The fishermen will lament, and all people who fish in the Nile will mourn, and people who spread nets on the waters will languish.
verses.after: Fishers will lament; all who cast hooks into the River will mourn; those spreading nets on the water will languish.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fishermen will lament, and all those who fish in the Nile will mourn, and those who spread nets on the waters will languish.

verses.rationale: Retain textile crafts and uncertainty in note.
verses.before: Moreover people who work in combed flax, and people who weave white cloth, will be confounded.
verses.after: Those working combed flax and weaving white cloth will be ashamed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover those who work in combed flax, and those who weave white cloth, will be confounded.

verses.rationale: Keep foundations text and workers’ distress.
verses.before: The pillars will be broken in pieces. All people who work for hire will be grieved in soul.
verses.after: Its foundations will be crushed; all wage workers will be sick at heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: The pillars will be broken in pieces. All those who work for hire will be grieved in soul.

verses.rationale: Retain elite ancestry boast and failed wisdom.
verses.before: The princes of Zoan are utterly foolish. The counsel of the wisest counselors of Pharaoh has become stupid. How do you say to Pharaoh, "I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?"
verses.after: Zoan’s princes are fools; Pharaoh’s wisest counselors give stupid advice. How can you tell Pharaoh, “I am a son of sages, a son of ancient kings”?
verses.tsw_comparator: The princes of Zoan are utterly foolish. The counsel of the wisest counselors of Pharaoh has become stupid. How do you say to Pharaoh, "I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?"

verses.rationale: Keep challenge and divine plan.
verses.before: Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you now; and let them know what the LORD of Hosts has purposed concerning Egypt.
verses.after: Where, then, are your wise men? Let them tell you, let them know what the **LORD** of hosts has planned against Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you now; and let them know what the LORD of Hosts has purposed concerning Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retain leaders as structural cornerstones.
verses.before: The princes of Zoan have become fools. The princes of Memphis are deceived. They have caused Egypt to go astray, who are the cornerstone of her tribes.
verses.after: Zoan’s princes have become fools; Memphis’s princes are deceived. The cornerstones of Egypt’s tribes have led it astray.
verses.tsw_comparator: The princes of Zoan have become fools. The princes of Memphis are deceived. They have caused Egypt to go astray, who are the cornerstone of her tribes.

verses.rationale: Keep divine mixing and graphic drunken image.
verses.before: The LORD has mixed a spirit of perverseness among her; and they have caused Egypt to go astray in all of its works, like a drunken man staggers in his vomit.
verses.after: The **LORD** has mixed a spirit of confusion into it. They make Egypt stagger in everything it does, as a drunk staggers in his vomit.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD has mixed a spirit of perverseness in the midst of her; and they have caused Egypt to go astray in all of its works, like a drunken man staggers in his vomit.

verses.rationale: Match head/tail and palm/reed extremes.
verses.before: Neither will there be for Egypt any work, which head or tail, palm branch or rush, may do.
verses.after: Egypt will have nothing that head or tail, palm branch or reed can accomplish.
verses.tsw_comparator: Neither will there be for Egypt any work, which head or tail, palm branch or rush, may do.

verses.rationale: Preserve gendered comparison without explanatory addition.
verses.before: On that day the Egyptians will be like women. They will tremble and fear because of the shaking of the hand of the LORD of Hosts, which he shakes over them.
verses.after: On that day Egypt will be like women, trembling and terrified before the hand that the **LORD** of hosts waves against it.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day the Egyptians will be like women. They will tremble and fear because of the shaking of the hand of the LORD of Hosts, which he shakes over them.

verses.rationale: Retain place-name fear and divine counsel.
verses.before: The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt. Everyone to whom mention is made of it will be afraid, because of the plans of the LORD of Hosts, which he determines against it.
verses.after: Judah’s land will become a terror to Egypt. Whenever anyone mentions it, Egypt will be afraid because of the plan the **LORD** of hosts is making against it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt. Everyone to whom mention is made of it will be afraid, because of the plans of the LORD of Hosts, which he determines against it.

verses.rationale: Keep five and pinned destruction, alternate Sun noted.
verses.before: On that day, there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the LORD of Hosts. One will be called "The city of destruction."
verses.after: On that day five cities in Egypt will speak Canaan’s language and swear allegiance to the **LORD** of hosts. One will be called City of Destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day, there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the LORD of Hosts. One will be called "The city of destruction."

verses.rationale: Retain two sacred markers and locations.
verses.before: On that day, there will be an altar to the LORD among the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the LORD at its border.
verses.after: On that day there will be an altar to the **LORD** in the heart of Egypt and a pillar to the **LORD** at its border.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day, there will be an altar to the LORD in the midst of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the LORD at its border.

verses.rationale: Preserve Egyptians as recipients of deliverance.
verses.before: It will be for a sign and for a witness to the LORD of Hosts in the land of Egypt; for they will cry to the LORD because of oppressors, and he will send them a savior and a defender, and he will deliver them.
verses.after: It will be a sign and witness to the **LORD** of hosts in Egypt. When they cry to the **LORD** because of oppressors, he will send them a savior and champion who will rescue them.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will be for a sign and for a witness to the LORD of Hosts in the land of Egypt; for they will cry to the LORD because of oppressors, and he will send them a savior and a defender, and he will deliver them.

verses.rationale: Keep reciprocal knowledge and cultic actions.
verses.before: The LORD will be known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know the LORD on that day. Yes, they will worship with sacrifice and offering, and will vow a vow to the LORD, and will perform it.
verses.after: The **LORD** will make himself known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know the **LORD** on that day. They will worship with sacrifice and offering, make vows to the **LORD**, and fulfill them.
