verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will be known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know the LORD in that day. Yes, they will worship with sacrifice and offering, and will vow a vow to the LORD, and will perform it.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated healing and judgment tension.
verses.before: The LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing. They will return to the LORD, and he will be entreated by them, and will heal them.
verses.after: The **LORD** will strike Egypt—striking and healing. They will return to the **LORD**, and he will answer their pleas and heal them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing. They will return to the LORD, and he will be entreated by them, and will heal them.

verses.rationale: Choose shared worship, note serve-Assyria ambiguity.
verses.before: On that day there will be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and the Assyrian will come into Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria; and the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians.
verses.after: On that day a highway will run from Egypt to Assyria. Assyrians will come to Egypt, and Egyptians to Assyria, and Egypt will worship with Assyria.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day there will be a highway out of Egypt to Assyria, and the Assyrian will come into Egypt, and the Egyptian into Assyria; and the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians.

verses.rationale: Retain three-way relationship and blessing.
verses.before: On that day, Israel will be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, a blessing among the earth;
verses.after: On that day Israel will be a third alongside Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth,
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day, Israel will be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth;

verses.rationale: Preserve startling three divine designations exactly.
verses.before: because the LORD of Hosts has blessed them, saying, "Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance."
verses.after: whom the **LORD** of hosts blesses, saying, “Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance.”
verses.tsw_comparator: because the LORD of Hosts has blessed them, saying, "Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance."

verses.rationale: Render Tartan as office; preserve Sargon and event.
verses.before: In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and took it;
verses.after: In the year the commander sent by Sargon king of Assyria came to Ashdod, fought against it, and captured it,
verses.tsw_comparator: In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and took it;

verses.rationale: Keep explicit naked sign act without softening.
verses.before: at that time the LORD spoke by Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, "Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your shoes from off your feet." He did so, walking naked and barefoot.
verses.after: the **LORD** spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz: “Go, loosen the sackcloth from your waist and take the sandals from your feet.” He did so, walking naked and barefoot.
verses.tsw_comparator: at that time the LORD spoke by Isaiah the son of Amoz, saying, "Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your shoes from off your feet." He did so, walking naked and barefoot.

verses.rationale: Retain three years and named targets.
verses.before: The LORD said, "As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a wonder concerning Egypt and concerning Ethiopia,
verses.after: The **LORD** said, “Just as my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years, a sign and wonder concerning Egypt and Cush,
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said, "As my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and a wonder concerning Egypt and concerning Ethiopia,

verses.rationale: Keep age range and humiliating exposure.
verses.before: so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, and with buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.
verses.after: so the king of Assyria will lead Egypt’s captives and Cush’s exiles, young and old, naked and barefoot, with buttocks exposed—Egypt’s nakedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, and with buttocks uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Retain failed political reliance.
verses.before: They will be dismayed and confounded, because of Ethiopia their expectation, and of Egypt their glory.
verses.after: They will be dismayed and ashamed of Cush, their hope, and Egypt, their pride.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will be dismayed and confounded, because of Ethiopia their expectation, and of Egypt their glory.

verses.rationale: Preserve local observers’ unresolved question.
verses.before: The inhabitants of this coast land will say on that day, 'Look, this is our expectation, where we fled for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria. And we, how will we escape?'"
verses.after: On that day the inhabitants of this coastland will say, ‘Look what has happened to our hope, to those we fled to for help and rescue from Assyria’s king! How, then, can we escape?’”
verses.tsw_comparator: The inhabitants of this coast land will say in that day, 'Look, this is our expectation, where we fled for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria. And we, how will we escape?'"

verses.rationale: Keep enigmatic title and desert storm.
verses.before: The burden of the wilderness of the sea. As whirlwinds in the South sweep through, it comes from the wilderness, from an awesome land.
verses.after: An oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea: Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negeb, it comes from the wilderness, from a fearsome land.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burden of the wilderness of the sea. As whirlwinds in the South sweep through, it comes from the wilderness, from an awesome land.

verses.rationale: Preserve repeated treachery and named attackers.
verses.before: A grievous vision is declared to me. The treacherous man deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam; attack! I have stopped all of Media's sighing.
verses.after: A harsh vision is told to me: “The betrayer betrays, the destroyer destroys. Advance, Elam! Lay siege, Media! I have put an end to all the groaning she caused.”
verses.tsw_comparator: A grievous vision is declared to me. The treacherous man deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam; attack! I have stopped all of Media's sighing.

verses.rationale: Retain prophet’s physical distress and birth simile.
verses.before: So my thighs are filled with anguish. Pains have taken hold on me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am in so much pain that I cannot hear. I so am dismayed that I cannot see.
verses.after: So my body is filled with anguish; pangs grip me like a woman in labor. I am bent over by what I hear, terrified by what I see.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore my thighs are filled with anguish. Pains have taken hold on me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am in so much pain that I cannot hear. I so am dismayed that I cannot see.

verses.rationale: Preserve desired twilight turned terror.
verses.before: My heart flutters. Horror has frightened me. The twilight that I desired has been turned into trembling for me.
verses.after: My heart reels; horror overwhelms me. The twilight I longed for has become a terror to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: My heart flutters. Horror has frightened me. The twilight that I desired has been turned into trembling for me.

verses.rationale: Retain abrupt banquet-to-battle shift, uncertain coverings noted.
verses.before: They prepare the table. They set the watch. They eat. They drink. Rise up, you princes, oil the shield!
verses.after: Set the table! Spread the coverings! Eat! Drink! Rise, commanders! Oil the shield!
verses.tsw_comparator: They prepare the table. They set the watch. They eat. They drink. Rise up, you princes, oil the shield!

verses.rationale: Keep commission and report instruction.
verses.before: For the Lord said to me, "Go, set a watchman. Let him declare what he sees.
verses.after: For this is what the Lord told me: “Go, post a lookout. Let him report what he sees.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Lord said to me, "Go, set a watchman. Let him declare what he sees.

verses.rationale: Retain paired riders, animals, doubled attention.
verses.before: When he sees a troop, horsemen in pairs, a troop of donkeys, a troop of camels, he will listen diligently with great attentiveness."
verses.after: When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs, riders on donkeys and riders on camels, let him listen intently, very intently.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When he sees a troop, horsemen in pairs, a troop of donkeys, a troop of camels, he will listen diligently with great attentiveness."

verses.rationale: Keep pinned lion, mark supplied like in note.
verses.before: He cried like a lion: "Lord, I stand continually on the watchtower in the daytime, and every night I stay at my post.
verses.after: He cried out like a lion: “Lord, I stand at the lookout all day long; I stay at my post every night.
verses.tsw_comparator: He cried like a lion: "Lord, I stand continually on the watchtower in the daytime, and every night I stay at my post.

verses.rationale: Preserve doubled fallen and unidentified shattering agent.
verses.before: Look, here comes a troop of men, horsemen in pairs." He answered, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the engraved images of her gods are broken to the ground.
verses.after: Look, here comes a troop of men, horsemen in pairs!” Then he answered, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon! All her gods’ carved images he has shattered to the ground.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, here comes a troop of men, horsemen in pairs." He answered, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the engraved images of her gods are broken to the ground.

verses.rationale: Keep tender yet violent threshing address.
verses.before: You are my threshing, and the grain of my floor!" That which I have heard from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.
verses.after: My threshed people, grain of my threshing floor, what I heard from the **LORD** of hosts, Israel’s God, I have told you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are my threshing, and the grain of my floor!" That which I have heard from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.

verses.rationale: Retain Dumah/Seir and repeated question.
verses.before: The burden of Dumah. One calls to me out of Seir, "Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?"
verses.after: An oracle concerning Dumah: Someone calls to me from Seir, “Watchman, how much of the night remains? Watchman, how much of the night?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The burden of Dumah. One calls to me out of Seir, "Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?"

verses.rationale: Keep ambiguous answer rather than optimistic resolution.
verses.before: The watchman said, "The morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire. Come back again."
verses.after: The watchman says, “Morning comes, and also night. If you want to ask, ask. Return; come again.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The watchman said, "The morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire. Come back again."

verses.rationale: Retain caravans and insecure lodging.
verses.before: The burden on Arabia. In the forest in Arabia you will lodge, you caravans of Dedanites.
verses.after: An oracle concerning Arabia: In Arabia’s thickets you will lodge, caravans of Dedan.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burden on Arabia. In the forest in Arabia you will lodge, you caravans of Dedanites.

verses.rationale: Keep practical refugee assistance and place.
verses.before: They brought water to the one who was thirsty. The inhabitants of the land of Tema met the fugitives with their bread.
verses.after: Bring water to meet the thirsty, inhabitants of Tema. Meet the fugitive with bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: They brought water to the one who was thirsty. The inhabitants of the land of Tema met the fugitives with their bread.

verses.rationale: Retain fourfold flight causes.
verses.before: For they fled away from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.
verses.after: They have fled from swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, from the weight of war.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they fled away from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.

verses.rationale: Preserve one contracted year.
verses.before: For the Lord said to me, "Within a year, as a worker bound by contract would count it, all the glory of Kedar will fail,
verses.after: For the Lord said to me, “Within one year, counted like a hired worker’s year, all Kedar’s glory will end.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the Lord said to me, "Within a year, as a worker bound by contract would count it, all the glory of Kedar will fail,

verses.rationale: Keep diminished military and divine seal.
verses.before: and the residue of the number of the archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, will be few; for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken it."
verses.after: The remaining archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be few.” The **LORD**, Israel’s God, has spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the residue of the number of the archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, will be few; for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken it."

verses.rationale: Retain title and questioning rooftop scene.
verses.before: The burden of the valley of vision. What ails you now, that you have all gone up to the housetops?
verses.after: An oracle concerning the Valley of Vision: What is happening to you, that all of you have climbed onto the roofs?
verses.tsw_comparator: The burden of the valley of vision. What ails you now, that you have all gone up to the housetops?

verses.rationale: Keep revelry amid nonbattle deaths.
verses.before: You that are full of shouting, a tumultuous city, a joyous town; your slain are not slain with the sword, neither are they dead in battle.
verses.after: You are full of uproar, a noisy city, a town of revelry. Your slain were not killed by the sword or did they die in battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: You that are full of shouting, a tumultuous city, a joyous town; your slain are not slain with the sword, neither are they dead in battle.

verses.rationale: Choose without-bow interpretation, note archers alternative.
verses.before: All your rulers fled away together. They were bound by the archers. Everyone who were found by you were bound together. They fled far away.
verses.after: All your leaders fled together; without a bow being drawn they were captured. All of you who were found were captured together, though you had fled far away.
verses.tsw_comparator: All your rulers fled away together. They were bound by the archers. All who were found by you were bound together. They fled far away.

verses.rationale: Preserve grief refusal and daughter image.
verses.before: So I said, "Look away from me. I will weep bitterly. Don't labor to comfort me for the destruction of the daughter of my people.
verses.after: So I said, “Look away from me; let me weep bitterly. Do not press me to be comforted over the devastation of my people’s daughter.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I said, "Look away from me. I will weep bitterly. Don't labor to comfort me for the destruction of the daughter of my people.

verses.rationale: Keep threefold chaos and acoustic landscape.
verses.before: For it is a day of confusion, and of treading down, and of perplexity, from the Lord GOD of Hosts, in the valley of vision; a breaking down of the walls, and a crying to the mountains."
verses.after: The Lord **GOD** of hosts has a day of tumult, trampling, and confusion in the Valley of Vision— walls battered down, cries reaching the mountains.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is a day of confusion, and of treading down, and of perplexity, from the Lord GOD of Hosts, in the valley of vision; a breaking down of the walls, and a crying to the mountains."

verses.rationale: Retain named forces and weapons.
verses.before: Elam carried his quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen; and Kir uncovered the shield.
verses.after: Elam carries the quiver, with chariots, men, and horsemen; Kir uncovers the shield.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elam carried his quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen; and Kir uncovered the shield.

verses.rationale: Keep strategic occupation.
verses.before: It happened that your choicest valleys were full of chariots, and the horsemen set themselves in array at the gate.
verses.after: Your finest valleys fill with chariots; horsemen take their stand at the gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: It happened that your choicest valleys were full of chariots, and the horsemen set themselves in array at the gate.

verses.rationale: Preserve exposed protection and named arsenal.
verses.before: He took away the covering of Judah; and you looked on that day to the armor in the house of the forest.
verses.after: Judah’s defenses are stripped away. On that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took away the covering of Judah; and you looked in that day to the armor in the house of the forest.

verses.rationale: Keep military inspection and water source.
verses.before: You saw the breaches of the city of David, that they were many; and you gathered together the waters of the lower pool.
verses.after: You saw the many breaches in David’s City and collected the water of the lower pool.
verses.tsw_comparator: You saw the breaches of the city of David, that they were many; and you gathered together the waters of the lower pool.

verses.rationale: Retain destruction as defensive tactic.
verses.before: You numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and you broke down the houses to fortify the wall.
verses.after: You counted Jerusalem’s houses and tore houses down to strengthen the wall.
verses.tsw_comparator: You numbered the houses of Jerusalem, and you broke down the houses to fortify the wall.

verses.rationale: Preserve preparations versus neglected Maker.
verses.before: You also made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you did not look to the one who had done this, neither did you have respect for the one who purposed it long ago.
verses.after: You made a reservoir between the two walls for the old pool’s water. But you did not look to its Maker or see the one who fashioned it long ago.
verses.tsw_comparator: You also made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you did not look to the one who had done this, neither did you have respect for the one who purposed it long ago.

verses.rationale: Retain four mourning actions.
verses.before: On that day, the Lord GOD of Hosts, called to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to dressing in sackcloth:
verses.after: On that day the Lord **GOD** of hosts called for weeping and mourning, shaved heads and sackcloth.
verses.tsw_comparator: In that day, the Lord GOD of Hosts, called to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to dressing in sackcloth:

verses.rationale: Keep contrary response and quoted fatalism.
verses.before: and look, joy and gladness, killing oxen and killing sheep, eating flesh and drinking wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die."
verses.after: But look—joy and revelry, killing cattle and slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine! “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”
verses.tsw_comparator: and look, joy and gladness, killing oxen and killing sheep, eating flesh and drinking wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die."

verses.rationale: Retain oath severity and both divine titles.
verses.before: The LORD of Hosts revealed himself in my ears, "Surely this iniquity will not be forgiven you until you die," says the Lord GOD of Hosts.
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts revealed this in my hearing: “Surely this guilt will not be atoned for until you die,” says the Lord **GOD** of hosts.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD of Hosts revealed himself in my ears, "Surely this iniquity will not be forgiven you until you die," says the Lord GOD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keep office, name, and commission.
verses.before: Thus says the Lord GOD of Hosts, "Go, get yourself to this treasurer, even to Shebna, who is over the house, and say,
verses.after: The Lord **GOD** of hosts says, “Go to this steward, to Shebna, who is in charge of the palace, and say:
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the Lord GOD of Hosts, "Go, get yourself to this treasurer, even to Shebna, who is over the house, and say,

verses.rationale: Retain repeated here and self-aggrandizing tomb.
verses.before: 'What are you doing here? Who has you here, that you have dug out a tomb here?' Cutting himself out a tomb on high, chiseling a habitation for himself in the rock!"
verses.after: ‘What do you have here? Whom do you have here, that you have cut yourself a tomb here—hewing your grave on a height, carving yourself a dwelling in the rock?
verses.tsw_comparator: 'What are you doing here? Who has you here, that you have dug out a tomb here?' Cutting himself out a tomb on high, chiseling a habitation for himself in the rock!"

verses.rationale: Keep sarcastic mighty address and force.
verses.before: Look, the LORD will overcome you and hurl you away violently. Yes, he will grasp you firmly.
verses.after: Look, the **LORD** is about to hurl you away, mighty man! He will seize you tightly,
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the LORD will overcome you and hurl you away violently. Yes, he will grasp you firmly.

verses.rationale: Preserve ball image, exile, and disgrace.
verses.before: He will surely wind you around and around, and throw you like a ball into a large country. There you will die, and there the chariots of your glory will be, you shame of your lord's house.
verses.after: wrap you round and round like a ball, and throw you into a broad land. There you will die, and there your splendid chariots will be—you disgrace to your master’s house!
verses.tsw_comparator: He will surely wind you around and around, and throw you like a ball into a large country. There you will die, and there the chariots of your glory will be, you shame of your lord's house.

verses.rationale: Retain first/third-person shift rather than harmonize.
verses.before: I will thrust you from your office. You will be pulled down from your station.
verses.after: I will thrust you from your office; he will pull you down from your position.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will thrust you from your office. You will be pulled down from your station.

verses.rationale: Preserve replacement’s full identity.
verses.before: It will happen on that day that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah,
verses.after: On that day I will call my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen in that day that I will call my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah,

verses.rationale: Keep transferred regalia and father metaphor.
verses.before: and I will clothe him with your robe, and strengthen him with your belt. I will commit your government into his hand; and he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.
verses.after: I will clothe him in your robe, bind your sash around him, and place your authority in his hand. He will be a father to Jerusalem’s inhabitants and the house of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: and I will clothe him with your robe, and strengthen him with your belt. I will commit your government into his hand; and he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.

verses.rationale: Retain shoulder-key and reciprocal authority.
verses.before: I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder. He will open, and no one will shut. He will shut, and no one will open.
verses.after: I will place the key of David’s house on his shoulder. What he opens, no one will shut; what he shuts, no one will open.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder. He will open, and no one will shut. He will shut, and no one will open.

verses.rationale: Keep peg/throne mixed imagery.
verses.before: I will fasten him like a nail in a sure place. He will be for a throne of glory to his father's house.
verses.after: I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will become a throne of honor for his father’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will fasten him like a nail in a sure place. He will be for a throne of glory to his father's house.

verses.rationale: Preserve familial load and vessel range.
verses.before: They will hang on him all the glory of his father's house, the offspring and the issue, every small vessel, from the cups even to all the pitchers.
verses.after: On him they will hang all the weight of his father’s house—offspring and offshoots, every small vessel, from bowls to every sort of jar.’
verses.tsw_comparator: They will hang on him all the glory of his father's house, the offspring and the issue, every small vessel, from the cups even to all the pitchers.

verses.rationale: Keep destabilizing ending and repeated firm peg.
verses.before: "On that day," says the LORD of Hosts, "the nail that was fastened in a sure place will give way. It will be cut down, and fall. The burden that was on it will be cut off, for the LORD has spoken it."
verses.after: On that day, declares the **LORD** of hosts, the peg driven into a firm place will give way, be cut down, and fall. The load hanging on it will be cut off, for the **LORD** has spoken.”
verses.tsw_comparator: "In that day," says the LORD of Hosts, "the nail that was fastened in a sure place will give way. It will be cut down, and fall. The burden that was on it will be cut off, for the LORD has spoken it."

verses.rationale: Retain maritime lament and news location.
verses.before: The burden of Tyre. Howl, you ships of Tarshish! For it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in. From the land of Kittim it is revealed to them.
verses.after: An oracle concerning Tyre: Wail, ships of Tarshish! It is devastated, without house or harbor. From the land of Kittim the news has been revealed to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The burden of Tyre. Howl, you ships of Tarshish! For it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in. From the land of Kittim it is revealed to them.

verses.rationale: Keep silent audience and merchants’ provision.
verses.before: Be still, you inhabitants of the coast, you whom the merchants of Sidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished.
verses.after: Be silent, coastland dwellers, whom Sidon’s merchants, crossing the sea, have filled.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be still, you inhabitants of the coast, you whom the merchants of Sidon, that pass over the sea, have replenished.

verses.rationale: Preserve Egyptian grain and international commerce.
verses.before: On great waters, the seed of the Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue. She was the market of nations.
verses.after: Across great waters came Shihor’s grain, the Nile’s harvest was her income; she became the nations’ marketplace.
verses.tsw_comparator: On great waters, the seed of the Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue. She was the market of nations.

verses.rationale: Retain sea’s maternal negation and both genders.
verses.before: Be ashamed, Sidon; for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying, "I have not labored, nor gave birth, neither have I nourished young men, nor brought up virgins."
verses.after: Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea, the sea’s fortress, has spoken: “I have not labored or given birth, raised young men or brought up young women.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Be ashamed, Sidon; for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying, "I have not labored, nor gave birth, neither have I nourished young men, nor brought up virgins."

verses.rationale: Keep Egyptian reaction to trade loss.
verses.before: When the report comes to Egypt, they will be in anguish at the report of Tyre.
verses.after: When the report reaches Egypt, they will writhe at the news of Tyre.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the report comes to Egypt, they will be in anguish at the report of Tyre.

verses.rationale: Retain departure and lament commands.
verses.before: Pass over to Tarshish! Wail, you inhabitants of the coast!
verses.after: Cross over to Tarshish! Wail, coastland dwellers!
verses.tsw_comparator: Pass over to Tarshish! Wail, you inhabitants of the coast!

verses.rationale: Keep ancient city and colonizing feet.
verses.before: Is this your joyous city, whose antiquity is of ancient days, whose feet carried her far away to travel?
verses.after: Is this your jubilant city, whose beginnings reach back to ancient days, whose feet carried her far away to settle?
verses.tsw_comparator: Is this your joyous city, whose antiquity is of ancient days, whose feet carried her far away to travel?

verses.rationale: Retain commercial and royal prestige.
verses.before: Who has planned this against Tyre, the giver of crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honorable of the earth?
verses.after: Who planned this against Tyre, the giver of crowns, whose merchants were princes, whose traders were honored across the earth?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who has planned this against Tyre, the giver of crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honorable of the earth?

verses.rationale: Keep divine planning and humiliation.
verses.before: The LORD of Hosts has planned it, to stain the pride of all glory, to bring into contempt all the honorable of the earth.
verses.after: The **LORD** of hosts planned it, to profane the pride of every splendor, to bring low all the earth’s honored people.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD of Hosts has planned it, to stain the pride of all glory, to bring into contempt all the honorable of the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserve river image and difficult restraint noun.
verses.before: Pass through your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish. There is no restraint any more.
verses.after: Flow across your land like the Nile, daughter Tarshish; there is no restraint anymore.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pass through your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish. There is no restraint any more.

verses.rationale: Keep hand, kingdoms, and Canaan.
verses.before: He has stretched out his hand over the sea. He has shaken the kingdoms. the LORD has ordered the destruction of Canaan's strongholds.
verses.after: He stretched his hand over the sea and shook kingdoms. The **LORD** gave orders concerning Canaan to destroy its strongholds.
verses.tsw_comparator: He has stretched out his hand over the sea. He has shaken the kingdoms. the LORD has ordered the destruction of Canaan's strongholds.

verses.rationale: Retain violated city image and failed refuge.
verses.before: He said, "You will rejoice no more, you oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon. Arise, pass over to Kittim. Even there you will have no rest."
verses.after: He said, “You will rejoice no more, oppressed virgin daughter Sidon. Rise, cross over to Kittim; even there you will find no rest.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, "You will rejoice no more, you oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon. Arise, pass over to Kittim. Even there you will have no rest."

verses.rationale: Choose Assyria-destroying reading, note difficult syntax.
verses.before: Look, the land of the Chaldeans. This people was not. The Assyrians founded it for people who dwell in the wilderness. They set up their towers. They overthrew its palaces. They made it a ruin.
verses.after: Look at the land of the Chaldeans! This people is no more. Assyria made it a home for desert creatures. They raised siege towers, stripped its palaces, and made it a ruin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the land of the Chaldeans. This people was not. The Assyrians founded it for those who dwell in the wilderness. They set up their towers. They overthrew its palaces. They made it a ruin.

verses.rationale: Match opening maritime refrain.
verses.before: Howl, you ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is laid waste!
verses.after: Wail, ships of Tarshish! Your stronghold is devastated.
verses.tsw_comparator: Howl, you ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is laid waste!

verses.rationale: Retain doubled seventy and comparison.
verses.before: It will come to pass on that day that Tyre will be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king. After the end of seventy years it will be to Tyre like in the song of the prostitute.
verses.after: On that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the lifetime of one king. At the end of seventy years, Tyre will be like the prostitute in the song:
verses.tsw_comparator: It will come to pass in that day that Tyre will be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king. After the end of seventy years it will be to Tyre like in the song of the prostitute.

verses.rationale: Preserve quoted song and memory reversal.
verses.before: Take a harp; go about the city, you prostitute that has been forgotten. Make sweet melody. Sing many songs, that you may be remembered.
verses.after: “Take a lyre, go round the city, forgotten prostitute! Play skillfully, sing many songs, so you may be remembered.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Take a harp; go about the city, you prostitute that has been forgotten. Make sweet melody. Sing many songs, that you may be remembered.

verses.rationale: Retain prostitution as international trade metaphor.
verses.before: It will happen after the end of seventy years that the LORD will visit Tyre, and she will return to her wages, and will play the prostitute with all the kingdoms of the world on the surface of the earth.
verses.after: At the end of seventy years the **LORD** will attend to Tyre. She will return to her earnings and prostitute herself with all the world’s kingdoms on the face of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will happen after the end of seventy years that the LORD will visit Tyre, and she will return to her wages, and will play the prostitute with all the kingdoms of the world on the surface of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keep surprising consecrated earnings and material uses.
verses.before: Her merchandise and her wages will be holiness to the LORD. It will not be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise will be for people who dwell before the LORD, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing.
verses.after: Yet her trade and earnings will be holy to the **LORD**. They will not be stored or hoarded; her trade will provide those who dwell before the **LORD** with abundant food and fine clothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her merchandise and her wages will be holiness to the LORD. It will not be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise will be for those who dwell before the LORD, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing.

comparative_references.scope: All 441 TSW verses read after independent drafting from each selected Hebrew record and all annotations. Shared wording retained where clear; overlap is triage only.
